biggest_gap.element: The loudness hierarchy in mix.wav / mix-hurt.wav is inverted. I measured every fed event's best 30 ms master-out RMS in the 80 ms after its tick against the 140 ms of bed before it. Under load (mix-hurt.wav, 67 events) the five QUIETEST events in the whole mix are: dodge -2.6 dB, dodgeEnd -1.4 dB, swing -0.3 dB, enemyAttack/brute +1.3 dB, enemyWindup/brute +1.4 dB. The five LOUDEST are hit/brute +15.1, kill/brute +15.1, playerHurt +14.9, enemyStagger +9.8, boltCut +9.8. Wave 1 ranks the same way (dodge -5.4, swing -0.9, enemyWindup +2.6 vs hit +9.6, kill +8.8). So every cause -- what you did to survive, and what is about to hurt you -- sits inside 2 dB of the bed, and every consequence sits 10-17 dB above it. The event map's gains confirm the intent: the two 'danger is coming' cues carry the two lowest gains in the table (enemyWindup caster laserRetro 0.12, spawnTelegraph lowFrequency_explosion 0.12) while the reward stack is 0.75 + 0.40. Cause: hit lives at +17.9 dB in 200-600 Hz, which is also where 40.5% of the mix's total energy already sits -- the busiest band is the one every cue needs.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: Both dense reference frames put the threat at the top of the hierarchy and the player's own confirmation below it. In ref-density-02 the incoming red/yellow bullet lattice is the single brightest object in a 1920x1080 frame; the player sprite and its muzzle flash are small and dim by comparison. In ref-density-01 the brightest pixel cluster in the frame is the fuse spark on the boss, i.e. the telegraph, not the hit that already landed. The professional exhibit spends its top 15 dB of headroom on the tell.
biggest_gap.fix: Re-rank the mix by cause, not consequence. (1) Raise the danger cues until enemyWindup and enemyAttack out-rank hit/kill in measured lift: target >= +10 dB best-band lift for windup under the 67-event render, with hit pulled back to about +8. Windup already has 20-28 ticks (333-466 ms) of runway before the attack, so it can afford a longer, louder cue. (2) Stop fighting for 200-600 Hz: give windup a reserved band (a pitched metallic ring at 2-4 kHz for brute, a rising tone for caster) and carve that band out of the bed and ambience with a static EQ notch rather than a duck. (3) Extend the duck stage so the windup, not only playerHurt and waveStart, can duck music + ambience -- a short -6 dB / 150 ms duck under the tell. Then re-measure with the same per-event lift script and require the ranked table to read danger cues above reward cues.

other_gaps: EVIDENCE LIMIT, stated plainly: exhibit B is three stills. Timing cannot be compared against it at all, and neither can any sound. I judged axis 3 against the acceptance criteria using our own tick-labelled event-timeline.json and the measured duck curves, not against the reference. Result: anticipation exists and is distinguishable from idle in the DATA (enemyWindup precedes enemyAttack by 20-28 ticks / 333-466 ms, consistently per enemy kind); there is exactly ONE readable contact (swing -> hit is 6 ticks / 100 ms, one impactPunch+impactPlate cluster, delay 0, and the impact lands on the tick damage becomes possible -- sample-accurate); the 'freeze' equivalent, the playerHurt duck, is 12 ms attack / 120 ms hold / -13 dB measured / back within 0.2 dB by the 667 ms i-frame window, which is long enough to register and short enough not to stall or pump; recovery settles on an exponential release with no pumping across four hits 120 ms apart (arbitration holds -13 dB flat, no stair-stepping). The single failure against the criteria is that the anticipation frame is not distinguishable from idle IN LEVEL (+1.4 dB), so the chain is fully present in the tick data and absent to the ear. Axis 3 = 4. Also note the two exhibits are not the same kind of work (an instrumented audio bundle vs retail game stills), so the blind framing was not actually blind.

AXIS SCORES 0-5 for exhibit A, all seven, so this round stays comparable: 1 Readability 2 (hierarchy inverted, above). 2 Material and light 3 (real impact stacking, limiter measured -5.37/-5.65 dBFS peak with 0 clipped samples and 0 samples >= 0.999, but 40.5% of energy in 200-500 Hz and 0.6% above 6 kHz -- no air, no reserved focal band). 3 Feel chain 4 (see evidence limit). 4 Composition 3 (bus graph, deeper-wins duck arbitration, 4-bar/2-bar bar-quantised layers and alive<=1 hysteresis are properly designed; nothing reserves a band or a moment for the focal event). 5 Sample integrity 4 (loop drift 0.006-0.0119 ms, 0 clipping, but see the ambience wrap seam below). 6 Density 2 (see below). 7 Originality 4 (measured duck arbitration plus hysteresis is its own design, not a Gungeon copy; the self-copy is enemy melee reusing the player's whoosh).

The dodge is the quietest event in the mix and has no audible confirmation at all. Element: dodge (cloth 0.70 @1.20 + woosh3 0.35 @1.40, both centred, no pan) measures -2.6 dB broadband under load and, banded, +2.0 dB at 60-200 Hz (bed rumble) with 0.0 / -3.9 / +0.7 / +0.1 dB at 200-600 / 600-1500 / 1500-4000 / 4000-10000 Hz. dodgeEnd is -1.4 dB broadband and negative in every mid band. There is no music at all in that render, so the dodge is inaudible over ambience and overlapping SFX alone. Stronger exhibit: in ref-density-02 the dodge-roll is legible as its own event even inside a full-screen bullet lattice. Fix: the dodge is a 216 ms window (13 ticks) with a distinct start and end -- give the start a sharp 3-6 kHz transient in a band nothing else occupies and the end a pitched-down 120 Hz thump, and require >= +6 dB best-band lift for both under the 67-event render.

The masking gate is aggregate-only and therefore blind to the two gaps above. It compares SFX p99 (-17.64 dB) against Music p50 and reports a pass at 6.8 dB (mix.wav) / 85.26 dB (mix-hurt.wav), but SFX p99 is carried entirely by hit, kill and the bells. My per-event measurement shows 41 of 67 events under 3 dB of lift (61%) and 23 under 1 dB, while the gate reads green. Fix: replace the single aggregate row with a per-event-type table -- median best-band lift for every type under the dense render, a floor of +6 dB in at least one octave band, and an explicit ordering assertion that danger cues rank above reward cues. Score the ordering, not just the floor.

mix-hurt.wav, the only dense render, has no music bed whatsoever: Music peak -87.93 dB, rms -102.81 dB, p99 -97.83 -- digital silence for the full 10 s. The worst-case event stream contains no waveStart or roomEnter, so the bed never starts. That means the bundle's headline claim (an adaptive bed with layer A/B crossfades and hysteresis) and the whole duck-under-density argument are untested in the only capture that has density, and the masking gate's 85.26 dB 'pass' measures the absence of the thing it is gating. The UI bus is likewise -999 dB (never fires) across 67 combat events. Fix: start the bed in the render harness before feeding worst-case events, or rebase the 10 s window so the wave-3 bell is inside it, then re-run all gates. Treat any gate whose margin exceeds about 40 dB as a failed measurement rather than a pass.

The enemy's melee attack and the player's own heavy swing are the same sample, 0.05 apart in pitch. Event map: swing (heavy) = woosh gain 0.80 pitch 0.80; enemyAttack brute = woosh gain 0.60 pitch 0.75; dodged = woosh gain 0.50 pitch 0.55. Three different meanings -- I attacked, it attacked, I was missed -- are one sample separated only by pitch and level, and the enemy's is the quieter of the first two. Stronger exhibit: in ref-density-01 the player's shot trail, the enemy projectiles and the boss's telegraph are three visually unrelated vocabularies (thin yellow line, discrete white orbs, orange fire plume). Fix: move enemy melee to a different sample family entirely (creature grunt plus a metal scrape) and keep woosh for the player only.

The ambience loop seam is the loudest discontinuity in the bundle: wrap step 0.024467 / 0.101634 against interior p99.99 of 0.368171 / 0.328482, i.e. 30.9% of an ordinary interior step, versus 7.3% for the bed and 0.8% for the drive. That is a repeating artefact every 11.428583 s in the layer that plays continuously and unmasked. Fix: match the ambience to what the drive already achieves -- crossfade the wrap over 30-50 ms or trim the loop to a matched zero crossing, and hold all three layers under about 5% of an interior step.

No capture in the bundle renders the density the reference shows. The busiest render is 67 events over 10 s (6.7/s); wave 1 is 3.9/s. ref-density-01 has roughly 30 simultaneous emitters on screen and ref-density-02 a full-screen bullet lattice. The bus graph asserts a voice cap of 4 starts per sound group per 70 ms with 38 ms stagger and a limiter meant to hold up under load, and neither is exercised: the limiter's measured peak is -5.65 dBFS, 4.65 dB of unused headroom, because nothing ever stacked. Fix: render a 30 s wave-3 mix with 300+ events (and a synthetic 200-simultaneous-start stress case), then re-run gates.png against it -- the clipping, masking and voice-cap rows only mean something at that density.

biggest_gap.element: mix-hurt.wav, the render labelled "worst case", and the two headline gates that rest on it. Its MUSIC bus measures peak -87.93 dB / rms -102.81 dB and its UI bus measures -999 dB: both are silent, because the captured window (ticks 1211-1793) contains no waveStart, no spawn and no roomClear, so the adaptive bed and the door cues never start. Three consequences, all measured: (a) I computed integrated loudness at -22.77 LUFS for mix-hurt against -20.25 LUFS for the ordinary wave-1 mix, so the peak-combat render is 2.5 dB QUIETER than the calm one, and peak combat is the quietest thing in the evidence; (b) gates.png reports the masking test as "85.26 dB gap (want >= 6)" in green, and it is green only because the music it measures against is off; (c) master peak is -5.65 dBFS against the limiter's own -3 dB threshold, so the limiter applied zero gain reduction in either render, and "clipping 0 samples, worst case" proves nothing about the limiter this piece was built around. The one component the bundle exists to prove has never been switched on in any capture it presents.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: ref-density-01 and -02 are the same test run on the eye, and they pass it at the peak. The frame with a boss, six enemies, two bullet trails, a smoke plume and twenty scattered casings is the BRIGHTEST and densest frame of the three, and it is still legible: density and level rise together, and the mechanism that stops the peak from breaking (the near-black floor holding the hot palette) is visibly doing work at that peak, not at rest. Nothing in the professional exhibit's hardest frame is missing or muted so the frame can be called clean.
biggest_gap.fix: Pre-roll the capture: fire roomEnter/waveStart before t0, let the bed loops reach steady state, then start recording, so the 67 worst-case events land over a running bed and a live UI bus. Re-render and re-derive both gates from that mix. Then spend the headroom: the current -5.65 dB peak leaves 4.6 dB before the limiter threshold, and taking it lands mix-hurt near -18 LUFS, inside the -16 to -18 LUFS band action games ship at, instead of 5 dB under it. Finally add the gate that is missing: worst case must show at least 1 dB of measured limiter gain reduction. Until a render engages the limiter, the limiter is a config listing, not a claim.

other_gaps: AXIS SCORES (all seven, this round). 1 Readability 3 - every sim event maps to a sound and threats carry pan+dist+itd, but the caster's tell is the second-quietest cue in the game. 2 Material and light (timbre + mix hierarchy) 3 - a real four-bus tree with every gain measured, but the hierarchy is only ever proven in a render whose music bus is off, and the whole bed sits at -20.25 LUFS. 3 Feel chain 3 - windup -> attack -> impact is present, the caster tell is a consistent 24 ticks (400 ms) ahead of boltFired across all five instances in the trace, and a killing hit layers four sounds against a non-killing hit's two. 4 Composition (stereo image and arrangement) 2 - the busier render is the narrower one, and playerHurt throws away the angle it is handed. 5 Pixel integrity (loop and sample-grid hygiene) 4 - 0 clipped samples, 0 samples at or above 0.999, loop drift 0.006-0.012 ms, seams measured against their own interior steps; the ambience seam is the lone outlier. 6 Density 2 - 3.9 events/s across the wave-1 file. 7 Originality 4 - a generated adaptive bed with no music files shipped, hysteresis on the layer gates, itd panning and a voice cap; a fan of the reference would not call this a copy.

EVIDENCE LIMIT, stated as required: the reference exhibits are three stills. Timing cannot be compared against them at all, so I judged axis 3 only against the feel-chain acceptance criteria and our own tick-labelled trace in event-timeline.json plus the onset positions in waveform.png. On those: the anticipation frame is distinguishable from idle (enemyWindup fires 24 ticks before boltFired for the caster, 18-27 ticks before enemyAttack for the brute); there is exactly one contact event per swing (each swing row is followed by exactly one hit row, 6 ticks later, never two); the freeze equivalent - the duck hold - is 120 ms, long enough to register and short enough not to stall; recovery overshoots and settles rather than snapping, the measured duck return passes -0.77 dB at 1.0 s and -0.01 dB by 1.5 s rather than stepping back to unity; and the peak lands on the tick damage becomes possible, since hit and kill share a tick and the four-layer kill stack is on the damage tick, not after it. I did not score axis 3 against the stills and no claim above is drawn from them.

The caster's tell has no timbre of its own. enemyWindup caster is laserRetro at gain 0.12, pitch 1.60. The bolt it warns about is laserRetro at gain 0.35, pitch 0.70. Same sample, 9.3 dB quieter, at the opposite end of the pitch range - the warning and the threat are one sound. Compare the brute, which gets swordMetal for the tell and woosh for the attack: two timbres, 4.7 dB apart. 0.12 is also the joint-quietest gain in the whole map alongside spawnTelegraph, beaten only by the footstep at 0.18. The caster is the ranged enemy, the one whose 400 ms tell is the entire reason to have audio for off-screen threats. Fix: give it its own sample - a rising charge, not the laser it fires - and take it to 0.30-0.35 so it clears the bed, then check it in a different band from the bolt.

The wave-1 render spends 45% of its length on nothing. All 39 events fall between t=0.50 s and t=5.45 s; ticks 328-448 carry zero sim events, and the SFX lane in waveform.png is flat from 6.0 s to 10.0 s. That is 3.9 events/s across the file against 7.9/s across the active span, presented as a 10 s combat capture. ref-density-01 puts roughly 25 live elements into one sixtieth of a second. Fix: window the capture on the busiest 10 s of the replay the way the worst-case one already does, or capture wave 3 - and if the sim genuinely produces a five-second hole after roomClear, that is the density finding, not the capture's.

The masking gate is constructed so it cannot fail. It compares SFX p99, the loudest 1% of windows, against Music p50, the median window. Run it honestly on the same levels.json numbers: SFX p50 -60.58 dB against Music p90 -20.65 dB, and the median 50 ms window has SFX 40 dB under loud music. Even the flattering version passes by 0.8 dB. Fix: make it per-event and take the minimum, not a percentile - for each of the 39 onsets compare the SFX 50 ms window at that onset against the music in the same window, and gate on the worst event. Band-limit it to 1-4 kHz, because a full-band RMS passes comfortably while a transient is buried under the bed's own midrange.

playerHurt is centred, and the event row carries the angle it was hit from. Every playerHurt row in event-timeline.json has an angle field (2.8696 at t=0.8667, 1.3510 at t=5.0667) and event-map.json marks the cue "no (centred)". Being hit from behind and being hit from the front sound identical. The same applies to dodge, which also carries an angle. This shows up in the measurement: I get side/mid at -2.3 dB for mix.wav but -5.74 dB for mix-hurt, so the image collapses toward mono in the busier render, exactly when there is the most to place, because in that window the player is doing most of the acting and everything the player does is centred. Fix: pan playerHurt by the incoming angle it already has, and pan the swing arc by its angle across the stroke rather than at a fixed point.

The ambience loop has the worst seam of the three and it is the only seam the render cannot show. gates.png measures the ambience wrap step at 30.9% of an ordinary interior step, against 7.3% for the bed and 0.8% for the drive - four times worse than the next-worst. Ambience is also the one loop that runs continuously and forever, and at 4 bars it wraps every 11.428 s, so in a 10 s render its seam never occurs. The only untested seam is the weakest one. Fix: render 25 s or trigger the wrap deliberately, and crossfade the ambience wrap until it sits with the other two.

The duck depth is quoted at three values and one of them is fiction. bus-graph.png labels the duck stage "ducked 0.2818 (-11 dB)" on both the music and the ambience path and states "depth -11 dB" in the duck box, but no scenario in duck-curves.json or gates.png ever reaches -11: playerHurt measures -13 dB and waveStart -9 dB, and those are the only two triggers that exist. -11 is a default that nothing uses, printed in the largest box on the page. Fix: label the stage with the two real depths, or delete the default.

restart is silent. event-map.json lists it "- silent -" next to poolOverflow, which is an internal condition, not an input. A player pressing restart gets no audio at all. I checked the other three silent rows before listing this one and they are all defensible: kill co-occurs on the same tick as a hit with killed=true, which plays four layers; enemyAttack caster co-occurs on the same tick as boltFired in all five instances in the trace. restart does not co-occur with anything. Fix: give it the roomEnter treatment, a bell plus the door, or state in the map why one input is deliberately mute.

The ducker pulls the room away, not just the music. The duck stage sits on ambience as well as music at the same -13 dB, 500 ms release, so the world recedes every time the player is hit - two hits in the worst-case 10 s is a full second of the room backing off. Music is what competes with a hurt sound; ambience is not, and it is already 13 dB down. Fix: route playerHurt's duck to music only, or take ambience to a -4 dB tap on the same envelope.

biggest_gap.element: The SFX bus is one flat fader with no priority tier, so danger cues do not survive density — and the gate that should catch it tests the wrong pair. enemyWindup/caster measures 30.0 dB best-band lift alone over the bed (solo-levels.json), but only 7.5 dB best-band and 3.1 dB broadband inside mix-hurt.wav (event-lift.json, n=9) — a 22.5 dB collapse. At that level it sits BELOW dodgeEnd (4.4 dB) and playerHurt (3.7 dB), and 1.9 dB above a footstep (1.2 dB). The whole stated hierarchy in solo-levels.json ('danger > player action > consequence > incidental') inverts at 10.8 events/s, which is the only density that matters. gates.png passes the masking test at 14.35 dB because it measures SFX p99 against Music p50; nothing in the bundle measures SFX against SFX, which is where the failure actually lives.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: ref-density-01 puts a boss, six flying enemies, two bullet trails, four impact bursts, smoke and eight loose pickups on one frame, and you still read the red boss as the thing that will hurt you — the professional exhibit reserves perceptual space for the threat and lets everything else lose it as density rises. Its threat cues stay legible precisely when the screen is fullest; ours are measured to become a footstep at exactly that moment.
biggest_gap.fix: Split danger cues (enemyWindup x3, enemyAttack x3, spawnTelegraph) onto their own bus and sidechain the ordinary SFX bus down 4-6 dB for the bell's decay window, the same way music already ducks under playerHurt. Then re-gate on lift measured in mix-hurt.wav, not solo: every danger cue must keep >= 6 dB broadband over the loudest concurrent non-danger SFX in the same 80 ms window. Add that SFX-vs-SFX row to gates.png; the current SFX-vs-Music row is passing while the mix fails.

other_gaps: TIMBRE HIERARCHY. All six in-combat danger cues are the same instrument at a different pitch: 'synth struck bowl' at 3000 / 2100 / 2200 / 2600 / 3200 / 2350 Hz, decays 0.16-0.8 s (event-map.json). One octave, one timbre, six meanings — and the spectrum confirms the pile-up: mix-hurt.wav's 2400-4800 Hz band sits at -2.8 dB rel, 6.3 dB above the next band, the single loudest region in the mix. The stronger exhibit gives each threat a different material (ref-density-01 reads a boss, a bullet and a shell casing as three different objects, not three pitches of one). Fix: one distinct timbre per enemy family — brute gets a low struck metal, charger a rising noise scrape, caster a tuned glass — and spread them across 400 Hz / 1.2 kHz / 3 kHz instead of stacking six bells in one octave.

NO INTENSITY ARC. mix-hurt.wav carries 2.8x the events of mix.wav (108 vs 39) and buys 3.2 dB at masterOut p99 (-14.04 -> -10.84) and 2.2 dB RMS (-22.15 -> -19.94). Crest factor is effectively identical: 17.4 dB vs 17.6 dB. A desperate wave-3 fight and a wave-1 mop-up have the same dynamic shape, one volume-knob notch apart. The reference pair spans a near-empty room (ref-density-03) and a screen-filling boss detonation (ref-density-01) — that is not a 3 dB difference. Fix: ride the SFX bus fader with alive-enemy count (or peak concurrent voices) over a 6-8 dB range, and lower the limiter's duty cycle so the loud fight has headroom to actually be loud rather than being flattened back to the quiet one.

DEAD TAIL. In mix.wav the SFX bus is at -180 dB — digital silence, not a low level — for the last 3.5 s after roomClear at ~6.3 s, and the UI bus goes silent after one doorOpen blip at ~7 s. 35% of the flagship capture has no event sound at all, carried by ambience at -21 dB. Silence as a bug: nothing marks the transition from 'fight over' to 'room breathing'. Fix: a post-clear room-tone motif or a decaying reverb tail on the last kill, so the tail is authored rather than absent.

PLAYERHURT DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON A DUCK THAT SOMETIMES HAS NOTHING TO DUCK. hurt4 at gain 0.16 and hitHelmet3 at 0.10 are the two lowest gains in the entire event map — 5x to 15x below everything else, which runs 0.24-2.20. Solo over the bed, playerHurt measures -2.9 dB broadband lift, BELOW the 'bed only (control)' row at 1.3 dB, which the file's own note defines as inaudible. It only reads in a mix because the -13 dB music duck opens a hole. But envelopes.json shows music at -22.0 dB (second 5) and -25.4 dB (second 10) in mix.wav — ducking that by 13 dB removes something already near the floor, so the cue vanishes exactly in the quiet moments where a single hit matters most. Fix: raise the hurt layer to carry its own 6+ dB lift with the duck disabled, then keep the duck as reinforcement rather than as the whole mechanism.

UI BUS IS DECLARATIVE, NOT REAL. bus-graph.png presents a four-bus mix (Music / Ambience / SFX / UI) with a -11 dB UI fader. Measured: UI is -999 dB — digitally silent for all 10 s of mix-hurt.wav — and in mix.wav carries exactly one sound, doorOpen_1 at roomClear. A bus that carries one door in 20 s of capture is a diagram entry, not a mix element. Fix: either give it the work it implies (low-HP heartbeat, HUD pickups, lock-on, menu) or fold it into SFX and stop drawing a fourth lane.

GATES MEASURE THE WRONG QUANTITIES. gates.png reports sample peak, RMS, clipping, and 'samples at or above 0.999 (inter-sample risk) 0/0'. Counting samples at full scale is not an inter-sample measurement — true peak needs 4x oversampled reconstruction, and a -2.36 dBFS sample peak through a 20:1 limiter can still overshoot 0 dBTP after codec/DAC reconstruction. There is also no loudness figure anywhere: no integrated or short-term LUFS (ITU-R BS.1770), which is the number a shipping mix is actually authored to. Fix: add LUFS-I and LUFS-S with a stated target, and replace the 0.999 sample count with a real 4x-oversampled dBTP reading.

THE MASKING THRESHOLD IS ASSERTED, NOT CALIBRATED. 'SFX p99 over Music p50: 10.05 dB gap (want >= 6)'. Nothing in the bundle derives the 6. This repo's own recorded lesson is to measure a threshold before asserting it. A gate whose pass line was chosen rather than measured will pass a mix that fails an ear — which is what is happening in the biggest gap above. Fix: run an A/B ladder to find the gap at which the cue stops being identifiable, then set the gate there and cite the run.

STATIC STEREO BIAS. Over the full 10 s, mix-hurt.wav is 1.9 dB right-heavy (L -21.0 / R -19.1 RMS) and mix.wav is 1.1 dB right-heavy, with L/R correlation 0.49 / 0.38 and side only -3.4 dB below mid. A whole capture of a fight that moves around the player should average near centre. Fix: confirm this is the replay's actual geography and not a pan-law error in the placement path; if it is geography, say so in levels.json so the next capture is comparable.

AXIS 3 IS UNEVIDENCED, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. event-timeline.json carries exact tick numbers for every event, and nothing in the bundle measures rendered audio onset against them. There is no onset-minus-tick figure, so it is unknown whether the contact sound lands on the damage tick or on the swing-start tick — the one alignment question the feel chain turns on. Fix: add an onset-detection row per event to event-lift.json reporting onset minus scheduled tick in ms, with a pass band of roughly +/- 1 tick (16.7 ms), and capture the matching tick-labelled visual strip so the audio peak can be checked against the frame the trace says damage becomes possible.

biggest_gap.element: playerHurt — the damage moment. In solo-levels.json it is the ONLY event in the whole map with a negative broadband lift: -2.9 dB against a bed of -31.2 dB (best-30ms -34.1 dB, i.e. below the bed it plays over). event-sound-map.png shows why: hurt4 plays at gain 0.16 and hitHelmet3 at 0.10 — the two lowest gains in the entire table — while the same event ducks music+ambience by -13 dB, the deepest duck in the game. So the mix's response to 'you just took damage' is a hole. The duck is doing the emphasis job the sound should be doing, and the result measures 4.2 dB below the bed-only control's own 1.3 dB false-positive floor.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-density-01 the impact IS the frame's peak. The room tiles never rise above mid-value; the contact is a white-hot core at full luminance with the sparks, smoke plume and blood arranged radially around it, and it owns a value band nothing else in the frame touches. The reference never signals danger by removing energy — the hurt/impact moment is the loudest, brightest, most saturated element present, and every other element is composed to point at it.
biggest_gap.fix: Make the hit carry the emphasis, not the duck. Raise hurt4 / hitHelmet3 until playerHurt measures >= +8 dB broad lift in solo-levels.json (from -2.9), and give it a 60-150 Hz thump so it lands in a band nothing else occupies — 20-80 Hz is currently -13.0 dB rel total while 11 of 22 cues pile into 2400-4800 Hz. Delay the -13 dB duck by ~80 ms so it opens the hole AFTER the transient rather than underneath it. Then re-run solo-levels and confirm the number actually moved; do not accept the change on the waveform alone.

other_gaps: EVIDENCE LIMIT, stated as required: the reference exhibits are stills, and they are VISUAL stills while exhibit A is audio. Timing cannot be compared against them at all, and neither can any audio property. Axis 3 below is judged only against the acceptance criteria, using our own tick-labelled event-timeline.json and the two rendered mixes. I say that plainly and did not grade feel against the references.

SEVEN AXES, exhibit A, this wave: 1 Readability 2 — wind-ups clear the bed by 5.0-7.9 dB, but playerHurt is -2.9, spawnTelegraph 0.6, enemyAttack/caster silent. 2 Material and light (timbre + level hierarchy) 2 — real bus tree and real limiter, but the spectral focal point is a 2400-4800 Hz pile-up (-3.0 dB rel total in mix-hurt) with a -13.2 dB scoop at 600-1200 and no low end. 3 Feel chain 2 — see the next row. 4 Composition 1 — see the mix-trajectory row. 5 Loop and sample integrity (the audio analog of pixel integrity) 4 — exhibit A's strongest axis. 6 Density 1 — see the onset-rate row. 7 Originality 3 — struck-bowl bells over impact samples is a distinct choice, borrowed from neither reference; not yet a voice.

AXIS 3 against the acceptance criteria, not the stills: anticipation PASSES — enemyWindup is distinguishable from idle (5.0-7.9 dB broad lift plus a -6 dB duck with a 150 ms release). ONE readable contact PASSES — swing fires woosh+swish once and hit is a separate later event, so there is no double-contact. Freeze length PASSES — duck-curves.json shows the -13 dB playerHurt duck back to -6.31 dB by ~0.7 s and -0.77 dB by 1.0 s, long enough to register and short enough not to stall, and four hits 120 ms apart hold at -13 and release once, so it does not pump. Recovery settle: exponential to zero with no overshoot, which is correct for a duck, so I do not penalise it. The axis FAILS on the last criterion only: the peak does not land on the damage tick. That is the biggest gap above.

Six events measure at or below the exhibit's own bed-only control. solo-levels.json states the control's broad lift is 1.3 dB and that 'any row at the control's level is inaudible in that band'. Measured: spawnTelegraph 0.6, footstep 1.2, boltCut 1.2, boltHitWall 1.3, dodgeEnd 1.4, enemyStagger 1.6, spawn 1.7. spawnTelegraph is the worst case because it is the head of the declared danger tier and it sits BELOW the control and below footstep. Stronger: in ref-density-01 the telegraph — the boss's charging bloom — is a saturated white-orange flare that reads before any other element in a 1920-wide frame. Fix: move spawnTelegraph's bell off 2350 Hz, where it competes with eleven other cues, down to 300-500 Hz, give it a 400 ms rising swell rather than a struck decay, and raise it until it measures >= +8 dB broad lift.

The declared hierarchy is not realised in the measurement. solo-levels.json states the intended order as danger > player action > consequence > incidental, but the measured broad lifts interleave: footstep (1.2, incidental) beats spawnTelegraph (0.6, danger); hit/charger (3.8, consequence) beats enemyWindup/charger (2.9, danger) and both enemyAttack rows (3.2, danger). Stronger: the references keep tiers on non-overlapping bands — in ref-density-03 the incoming laser is full-saturation green, the enemies are mid-saturation, the furniture is desaturated, and no prop ever brightens past a threat. Fix: set gains from the measured lift rather than from each sample's nominal gain, and iterate until the four tiers occupy disjoint lift ranges (danger >= 8 dB, player action 5-7, consequence 3-5, incidental 1-3).

Band crowding. 11 of the 22 rows in solo-levels.json report bestBand 2400-4800 Hz, and my FFT of mix-hurt.wav confirms that band is the single loudest in the spectrum at -3.0 dB rel total, against -13.2 dB at 600-1200 Hz and -13.0 dB at 20-80 Hz. Worst-case combat is a top-mid pile-up with no floor under it, so cues mask each other exactly where the ear is most fatigued. Stronger: ref-density-01 spans its full value range in one frame — near-black room, mid-value tiles, saturated mid-tone enemies, one white core — so nothing competes for the same register. Fix: assign each tier a band and hold it. Hits and kills 60-200 Hz, wind-ups 300-800 Hz, player actions 1-2 kHz; stop pitching every synth struck bowl between 2100 and 3200 Hz.

Bed density. From envelopes.json I counted onsets (a >6 dB rise over 50 ms, above -40 dBFS): the MUSIC bus produces 2 onsets in 10 seconds, and both are the loop's own downbeat at 0.50 s and 5.45 s. AMBIENCE produces 0 onsets in 10 s. The music envelope decays monotonically about 15 dB across each 5.71 s loop (-13 dB at the top to -25 dB at the bottom, per 0.25 s bin) and only re-strikes at the loop wrap, so the 'pulse' layer at +2 dB and 'churn' at -1.5 dB that bus-graph.png advertises produce no measurable beat-rate modulation at all. At 84 bpm a beat is 0.714 s, so the bed has one onset per eight beats. Stronger: ref-density-02 and -03 have continuous motion filling every part of the frame; nothing in them decays to stillness. Fix: put a real onset on every beat in layer A so the bed is a pulse rather than a ring-out, and verify with the same onset count, not by ear.

SFX density is losing 5 events in 6. The same onset count gives the SFX bus 8 onsets in 10 s (0.8/s) while event-timeline.json feeds 39 events (3.9/s); in the worst case, 108 events (10.8/s) yield 13 SFX onsets (1.3/s) and only 4 at the master (0.4/s). Combat smears into a continuous wash instead of resolving as discrete hits. Fix: shorten the attack on the impact samples and widen the 38 ms same-instant stagger to a value that keeps simultaneous hits separable, then re-count onsets and require the SFX rate to track the event rate rather than flatten against it.

Mix trajectory. My 100 ms RMS envelope of mix.wav falls monotonically from -15.3 dB at 0.5 s to -33.8 dB at 9.9 s. The loudest moment of an entire cleared wave is the waveStart bell before any fighting happens, and the mix decays 18 dB away from it. Master peak is -4.72 dB, so the -3 dB limiter never engages and 4.7 dB of headroom is unused. Stronger: ref-density-01 and -02 are both captured at the fight's peak, and the composition escalates toward it. Fix: drive an intensity ramp from alive-enemy count and remaining HP so level rises into the wave clear; target the last second of a wave louder than its first.

Four events are silent by design and at least two of those are defects. event-sound-map.png lists kill, enemyAttack/caster, restart and poolOverflow as '— silent —'. enemyAttack/caster is the caster committing to a shot, the one enemy action the player must read at range, and it emits nothing of its own — there is no enemyAttack/caster row in solo-levels.json to measure. restart produces no sound at all, and the UI bus measures -999 dB across the entire 10 s of mix-hurt.wav despite a -11 dB fader. Silence in response to an input is a defect, not restraint. Fix: give enemyAttack/caster a short pre-bolt cue distinct from boltFired, and put restart on the UI bus.

Evidence defect, worth fixing because the exhibit IS the evidence: in event-lift.json, waveStart and spawnTelegraph report byte-identical figures (25.5 dB broad, 43.9 dB in 1200-2400), and kill/brute, waveClear and roomClear report another identical triple (5.8 dB broad, 12.7 dB in 80-200). Those events co-occur in the replay, so the in-mix lift metric cannot attribute anything to an individual event when two land in one window — it silently credits both with the louder one's lift. solo-levels.json is the honest measurement and it is what exposed the playerHurt defect; event-lift.json as published invites the opposite read. Fix: drop rows whose measurement window overlaps another event, or label them 'shared window' so no one grades a cue on a neighbour's number.

One blemish on the otherwise strong integrity axis: gates.png reports the ambience loop's wrap step at 30.9% of an ordinary interior step (0.024467 / 0.101634 against an interior p99.99 of 0.368171 / 0.328482), against 7.3% for the bed and 0.8% for the drive. The ambience seam is four times the bed's and it repeats every 11.43 s. Fix: crossfade the ambience wrap or trim it to a zero crossing until it measures under 10% like the other two.

biggest_gap.element: The heavy swing. In event-sound-map.png the heavy swing is the light swing pitched DOWN (woosh 1.00 @0.80 + swish 1.06 @0.95 / 170 ms, against light's woosh 0.78 @1.10 + swish 0.85 @1.35 / 110 ms). The exhibit's own solo-levels.json, measured against the bed-only control with nothing else playing, gives light swing broadLift 3.0 dB / best30 -28.2 dB / bestLift 20.3 dB and heavy swing broadLift 3.0 dB / best30 -28.2 dB / bestLift 19.6 dB. Identical broadband, and the heavy is 0.7 dB WEAKER in its best band, because pitching down moves its energy out of 2400-4800 Hz where the bed is thinnest. Inside mix.wav the two heavy swings (tick 185 / 3.083 s and tick 313 / 5.217 s) measure -0.0 dB and -0.8 dB of 30 ms RMS lift over the preceding 140 ms of bed - at or below the bed. A spectral-flux onset detector that finds a transient at 28 of the 32 event times in mix.wav finds neither heavy swing; both are in the miss list. The player's committed, higher-cost attack is the one input in the whole bundle that produces no measurable onset, twice out of two.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-density-01 the single most consequential thing in the frame - the rocket detonating on the boss - is also the largest, brightest and highest-contrast element by a wide margin, with a white core, a full smoke plume and its own light spill. Every lesser event in the same frame (drifting hearts, shell casings, the blob enemies, the yellow tracers) is smaller, dimmer and lower-contrast. ref-density-02 does the same with the star-shaped bullet pattern: at maximum density the frame still has one unambiguous focal element, and weight sets the hierarchy. Gungeon never lets the heavy hit read the same as an incidental one, and never makes the big version of an effect the quiet version of the small one.
biggest_gap.fix: Stop deriving the heavy swing by pitch-shifting the light one. Give it a component the light swing does not have: keep a low body layer for weight, but add a bright 2400-4800 Hz transient/click layer on top so the heavy gains presence instead of trading it away. Gate it - re-run solo-levels.json and require heavy swing bestLift >= light swing bestLift + 6 dB and broadLift >= +6 dB over the bed-only control, and require the onset detector to fire at both heavy-swing ticks in mix.wav. Then spend the ducking machinery the bundle already has (currently reserved for danger cues) on the heavy swing alone: a shallow -3 dB / 120 ms release duck so the bed steps out of the player's biggest commitment. Light swing stays as-is; the asymmetry has to be built into the heavy, not the light.

other_gaps: EVIDENCE LIMIT, stated plainly: the reference exhibits are three stills. Timing cannot be compared against them, and I did not try. I judged axis 3 against the acceptance criteria using our own tick-labelled trace (event-timeline.json) and the rendered mixes only. Result: anticipation IS distinguishable from idle (enemyWindup at tick 118 lands 23 ticks / 383 ms before enemyAttack at tick 141, carries +33.0 dB of 2400-4800 Hz lift in mix.wav and fires its own -6 dB / 150 ms duck). There is exactly ONE contact beat per swing (swing tick 121 -> hit tick 127, 100 ms, no double-trigger anywhere in the 39-event stream). The freeze analogue - the playerHurt duck at -13 dB, 80 ms delay, 120 ms hold, 420 ms release - is long enough to register and is back within 0.2 dB before the 667 ms i-frame window closes, so it does not stall. Two criteria FAIL. Recovery does not overshoot and settle: duck-curves.png shows a pure asymptote (-1.29 dB at 1.00 s, -0.01 dB by 1.75 s) with no settle-past-and-return on any of the five cases. And the peak does not land on the tick damage becomes possible: at tick 127 the hit measures -0.0 dB broadband lift, while the enemy's windup at tick 118 measures +3.2 dB - the loudest moment of the player's own attack chain is the enemy telegraph, not contact.

The exhibit ships no tick-labelled frame strip, so the visual half of the feel-chain acceptance criteria (an anticipation frame, one contact frame, freeze length, recovery overshoot) is unanswerable from this bundle at all - only its audio analogue is. waveform.png already carries an event ruler with tick-derived times. The stronger exhibit is a frame: it answers readability, hierarchy and contact in a single still with no companion file. FIX: render a strip of the same replay window, labelled with the same ticks as event-timeline.json, on the same x-axis as waveform.png, so a judge can put the visual peak and the audio peak on one tick line.

Stated hierarchy vs measured hierarchy. solo-levels.json declares 'danger (wind-up, attack, telegraph) > player action > consequence > incidental', then measures the exact inversion at both ends and ships it as a note. playerHurt - a consequence - is rank 1 at 12.8 dB broadLift / 31.2 dB bestLift, above every danger cue. spawnTelegraph - the one cue that says something is about to arrive - measures 0.6 dB broadLift, BELOW the bed-only control's 1.3 dB. In ref-density-03 the threat (the boss filling the top third, its muzzle flash, the green beam) is the loudest thing in the frame and the player's own status readouts are the dimmest; the declared hierarchy and the rendered one are the same hierarchy. FIX: put the intended rank column next to the measured rank in solo-levels.json and make any inversion a gates.png FAIL, not prose.

Three events measure identical to the bed-only control and are therefore inaudible by the bundle's own definition ('any row at the control's level is inaudible in that band'). Control: broad 1.3 / best30 -29.9 / peak -17.0. footstep: 1.3 / -29.9 / -17.0. boltHitWall: 1.2 / -30.0 / -17.0. enemyStagger: 1.1 / -30.1 / -17.0. All three match to the tenth of a dB on all three figures. enemyStagger is combat feedback - the player lands a stagger and the mix returns literally nothing measurable. This is silence as a bug, not restraint. FIX: enemyStagger needs a distinct short cue clearing the control by >= 6 dB; footstep and wall hits may stay incidental but must clear it by ~3 dB or be deleted from sfxMap so voices stop being spent on nothing.

The wave-1 climax stacks four events on one tick - hit, kill, waveClear and roomClear all at tick 327 - and roomClear alone fires three 'synth struck bowl' bells (261.63, 392, and a +0.45 s tail) plus doorOpen. Six bells of ONE synth timbre inside one moment, all centred, no pan, no stagger except doorOpen's +1.2 s. event-lift.json cannot separate them: kill/brute, waveClear and roomClear all report exactly 6.5 dB broad and 13.2 dB in 80-200 Hz - the measurement is reading one sound three times. The reference's densest frame (ref-density-02, a full-screen bullet star) still resolves into distinct readable strands. FIX: stagger the victory chain the way doorOpen already is - kill at 0, waveClear +250 ms, roomClear bell +600 ms - and give them three different timbres, not three pitches of one bowl.

The limiter, not the design, is setting the level of every transient in the busy mix, and the bundle does not report it. bus-graph.png: threshold -3 dB, ratio 20:1, attack 3 ms. In mix-hurt the pre-limiter SFX bus peaks at -2.22 dB and master out lands at -2.36 dB, so the limiter is engaged across the whole combat section. gates.png reports 'clipped 0 samples' and stops there. Zero clipping is not evidence the hits survived. FIX: add a gain-reduction trace to gates.png - max GR, p99 GR, and percent of the render under >1 dB reduction - and gate it, so a hit that got flattened by 6 dB shows up as a number.

Density holds up in count but not in delivery. mix.wav is 39 events over 448 ticks (5.2 events/s) and mix-hurt 108 over 10 s (10.8/s), against the reference stills' roughly 25-35 discrete simultaneous elements per frame - so the raw rate is in range. But my onset detector matches only 56 of 70 distinct event times in mix-hurt: one event in five produces nothing detectable at high density, and the misses cluster at 7.28-7.37 s and 8.2-8.7 s, exactly where events pile up. The reference frames stay readable AT density; ours degrades with it. FIX: make 'onsets detected / event times fed' a gate in gates.png and hold it above 0.90 in mix-hurt.

The top octave is missing. In mix.wav the 5120-10240 Hz band sits at -19.9 dB and 10240-20000 Hz at -28.1 dB relative to total; in mix-hurt, -21.6 and -30.0 dB. There is effectively no air. Under load the mix also loses its middle: 320-640 Hz drops from -6.6 to -14.1 dB and 640-1280 Hz from -8.4 to -16.1 dB relative, collapsing everything into a 1.3-5 kHz shelf. The reference stills carry hard specular highlights at the very top of their value range (the white core of the explosion, the yellow tracer edges) against a fully-populated midtone; ours is a mid shelf with no highlight and a hollowed midrange. FIX: check whether the pitched-down Kenney sources still have top-octave content at all, and add a synthesized click/air layer to the impact family so the brightest events actually reach the top band.

Ambience has a measurably worse loop seam than either music layer, on the one bus that plays continuously and is never masked by combat. gates.png: ambience wrap step is 30.9% of an ordinary interior step; bed is 7.3% and drive 0.8%. FIX: crossfade the ambience wrap or re-trim it until its wrap step matches the bed's ~7%.

Placement is claimed but never proven. event-sound-map.png marks most world sounds 'yes (pan + dist + itd)', yet no image or JSON in the bundle measures a pan law, a distance rolloff curve, or an ITD in samples. The bundle proves level and ducking to three decimal places and proves position not at all - and mid/side on mix.wav comes out at -4.7 dB side-to-mid with L/R correlation 0.50, unusually wide for a top-down game mix and unexplained anywhere. FIX: add a pan-sweep render - one sound at nine x positions across the arena - with measured L/R level difference and ITD per position, alongside the duck curves that already get this treatment.

biggest_gap.element: The danger channel has one timbre. Per event-sound-map.png, six of the game's danger cues — enemyWindup brute (3000 Hz), caster (2100 Hz), charger (2200 Hz), enemyAttack brute (2600 Hz), charger (3200 Hz) and spawnTelegraph (2350 Hz) — are all the same 'synth struck bowl', and the whole vocabulary fits inside 2100-3200 Hz, a span of 7.3 semitones. solo-levels.json confirms the ear cannot separate them: all six peak in the same 2400-4800 Hz band, and the six-band lift profiles are near-identical after removing loudness — enemyAttack/brute vs enemyAttack/charger 0.6 dB rms apart, enemyWindup/charger vs spawnTelegraph 1.8 dB, enemyWindup/brute vs enemyWindup/charger 2.0 dB. Only the caster wind-up separates at all (5.7 dB). Worse, the layer that actually says WHICH enemy is the quiet one: bell 1.20 vs swordMetal 0.30 (-12.0 dB) for the brute, 0.72 vs laserRetro 0.22 (-10.3 dB) for the caster, 1.07 vs creature 0.28 (-11.6 dB) for the charger. The identifying cue sits 10-12 dB under the generic cue, on all three. Result: with your back turned you hear 'something is about to hurt me' but never which of three enemies, and the three demand different responses.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-density-01 and -02 the threat channel is separated by carrier, not by an offset on one shared carrier. The yellow tracer line, the red laser sight, the orange fireball cluster, the pink hearts and the grey smoke each own a different hue AND a different shape AND a different motion, at full contrast. The identifying property is the loud property — you never have to look past a generic 'danger' element to find out which danger it is. Nothing in that frame is another thing shifted one semitone.
biggest_gap.fix: Give each enemy class its own timbre family and separate them by more than an octave, then invert the layer ratio. Concretely: keep the struck bowl for exactly one class, move the brute to a low struck/wood body around 300-500 Hz, and give the charger a rising pitch sweep (not a struck decay) so it is separated by envelope shape as well as by frequency; leave the caster's bright bell where it is. Then raise the identifying layer (swordMetal / laserRetro / creature) to within 3 dB of the shared layer, or above it, and drop the shared bell to a 'something' bed underneath. Re-run solo-levels.json and require the six-band shape distance between any two danger cues to be >= 8 dB rms before calling it done — that number is the gate, not the ear.

other_gaps: EVIDENCE LIMIT, stated plainly: Exhibit B is three stills, so no timing in Exhibit A was compared against it. Axis 3 was judged against the acceptance criteria using our own tick-labelled event-timeline.json and the measured duck-curves.json only. What that trace shows: anticipation is present and distinguishable (light swing tick 121 -> hit 127 = 100 ms; heavy swing 185 -> hit 199 = 233 ms; enemy wind-up 118 -> attack 141 = 383 ms of telegraph, a real reaction window). Contact is a single readable event (one 'hit' per swing, kill is deliberately silent and folded into hit-killing's four layers, so there is no double contact). The 'freeze' analogue — the playerHurt duck — reaches -13 dB 122 ms after the event and is back within 0.2 dB by 1.0 s: long enough to register, short enough not to stall. Recovery overshoots and settles rather than snapping (duck-curves.png shows an exponential release with no step). SEVEN-AXIS SCORE for Exhibit A this round: 1 Readability 1/5. 2 Material and light (timbre and spectral hierarchy) 2/5. 3 Feel chain 3/5. 4 Composition (mix arrangement over time) 3/5. 5 Pixel integrity (seam and artifact integrity) 4/5. 6 Density 2/5. 7 Originality 3/5.

A full-gain wind-up bell rings for an enemy that is already dead, on 2 of 2 kills in the trace. event-timeline.json: enemyWindup id=2 at tick 193, kill id=2 at tick 199; enemyWindup id=1 at tick 321, kill id=1 at tick 327. The wind-up bell is gain 1.20, the loudest single SFX in the game, and it has a 0.3 s decay, so on every kill the last thing the player hears is a maximum-urgency danger cue for a threat that no longer exists — and 'kill' itself is mapped '- silent -', so nothing masks it. The reference frames never leave a threat marker attached to a dead thing. Fix: cancel or fast-fade (30 ms) the wind-up voice on the kill event, and add a stop() path for looping/decaying danger voices keyed to entity id.

Four events fire and are measurably inaudible — silence that costs CPU. solo-levels.json control row is broad 1.3 / best30 -29.9 / peak -17.0. footstep reports 1.3 / -29.9 / -17.0, identical to the control in every figure. enemyStagger -30.1 / -17.0, boltHitWall -30.0 / -17.0, boltCut -30.0 / -16.8 — all within 0.2 dB of the control. So walking, staggering an enemy, cutting a bolt and a bolt hitting the wall produce no measurable sound during combat. Player movement in particular is a held input with zero audible response. The reference gives every interaction a visible mark (casings, ricochet rings, wall scorch). Fix: for the four, raise gain until best30 clears the control by >= 6 dB, or cut them and spend the budget elsewhere — but do not ship a play() call that measures at the noise floor.

Four events have no sound at all, and one of them is a player input. event-sound-map.png lists 'kill', 'enemyAttack caster', 'restart' and 'poolOverflow' as '- silent -'. kill and enemyAttack caster are defensible (covered by hit-killing and boltFired). 'restart' is not: the player presses a key and the game answers with nothing. Fix: give restart a UI-bus confirm (it is the one bus that is idle anyway) and a hard cut of all decaying voices, so the press reads as a state change.

Worst-case combat piles 56.9% of all spectral energy into 2400-4800 Hz. Measured by FFT over the whole of mix-hurt.wav: 20-80 Hz 6.7%, 80-200 11.1%, 200-600 8.9%, 600-1200 2.6%, 1200-2400 12.3%, 2400-4800 56.9%, above 4800 1.2%. That is the band the ear is most sensitive to, and it is where all six struck-bowl bells live — so the busiest moment in the game is also the most fatiguing, and every new cue lands on top of the existing pile. mix.wav has the mirror problem: 53.2% in 200-600 Hz, a boxy midrange lump. Fix: fixing the biggest gap above (spreading the bell family by octaves) fixes most of this; then check the band histogram again and require no single octave band above ~30%.

There is no top end. Above 4800 Hz: 1.17% of energy in mix.wav, 1.11% in mix-hurt.wav. Above 12 kHz: 0.09% and 0.05%. The reference frames carry a whole layer of small bright detail — shell casings, glass sparkle, ricochet glints — that reads as 'expensive'. Fix: add a short bright transient layer (2-4 ms, 6-10 kHz noise burst) on hit, dodge and boltCut. It costs almost nothing in RMS and is the cheapest available lift in perceived production value.

The player's hit confirm is the weakest link in the chain the game is about. solo-levels.json: hit/brute broad lift 3.0 dB, best band 200-600 at 9.8 dB, peak -16.7 dB — against enemyWindup/brute at 28.1 dB best-band lift. The confirmation that your sword landed reads 18 dB less prominent than the enemy telling you it is about to swing. The stated hierarchy in solo-levels.json ('danger > player action > consequence') is itself the defect for a one-sword melee slice: contact IS the payoff. Fix: promote hit above the wind-up in the best-band lift table — target >= 20 dB best-band lift — by adding the bright transient layer above and a short low body thump, and pull the wind-up bells down as the timbre spread makes them readable at lower gain.

The SFX bus is at digital silence for 41% of the wave-1 render. Envelope analysis of mix.wav: sfx below -55 dBFS from 5.89 s to 10.0 s continuously, plus 3.65-4.05 s; 50.9% of the whole render is below -55 dBFS, and levels.json gives the SFX 50 ms p10 as -99 dB (true zero). Master out falls from -24 dB to -33 dB after room clear and stays there. Against Exhibit B, where a single frame carries roughly forty simultaneous discrete elements and something is always firing, ricocheting or burning, our post-clear room is one door creak and then nothing. Fix: this is the density axis — give the cleared room a life layer (occasional prop settle, torch crackle, distant drip on the ambience bus, pickup shimmer) so the SFX bus floor never sits at -99, and make footsteps audible (see above) so player movement fills the gap.

The music tail ends in a step, not a fade. 100 ms RMS on mix.wav: -28.3 (8.9 s), -28.9 (9.0 s), -32.9 (9.1 s) — a 4 dB drop in one 100 ms window, with nothing under it. bus-graph.png declares 'crossfade in 1.1 s / out 2.2 s', so this is a layer ending on a bar boundary rather than crossfading. Fix: hold the exploration bed under the combat layers so the crossfade lands on something, and check the 100 ms RMS curve for steps > 1.5 dB after the change.

The ambience loop seam is measurably audible where the other two are not. gates.png: ambience wrap step 0.024467 / 0.101634 against interior p99.99 of 0.368171 / 0.328482 = 30.9% of an ordinary step. bed is 7.3% and drive 0.8%. So every 11.43 s the ambience produces a discontinuity roughly a third of a normal sample step — the one loop in the mix that can tick. Fix: trim the ambience loop to a zero crossing or overlap-crossfade the last 20 ms, then re-run the gate and get it under 10% like the other two.

A whole asset class is dead. gates.png: 'announcer resident or playable — none, 8 files skipped at load'. Eight files ship or half-ship and zero are playable. Fix: either wire them to real events (wave start, room clear, low HP) or delete them from the manifest; a permanently-skipped load path is a landmine, not a feature.

The UI bus is effectively unused, and it is the one that should be warning you. levels.json: in mix.wav the UI bus peaks at -14.97 dB with 50 ms p50 of -99 (one doorOpen in ten seconds); in mix-hurt.wav — the 108-event worst case with the player taking damage — UI peak is -999 dB, i.e. absolute digital silence for the full ten seconds. Nothing tells the player they are close to death while playerHurt is the loudest event in the game. Fix: put a low-HP pulse and a dodge-ready tick on the UI bus. It sits outside the duck (bus-graph.png: duck applies to music+ambience only), so it will cut through combat without any further mix work.

The in-mix per-event measurement cannot separate co-timed events, and the report does not say so. event-lift.json gives waveStart and spawnTelegraph byte-identical figures (broad 25.5; bands 16 / 25.1 / 34.8 / 43.9 / 41 / 29.1) because both fire at tick 30, and kill/brute, waveClear and roomClear are likewise identical to each other. So several rows of that table are not measuring the event they are labelled with. Everything else in this pack labels its own limits carefully (the worktree-dirty note, the 'measured not computed' headers, the 'no image can judge whether the bed sounds good' line) — this one omission is out of character. Fix: drop or asterisk any row whose 80 ms window contains another event, or widen the separation requirement and report n after filtering.

The pack cannot answer its own feel-chain acceptance criterion. There is no tick-aligned strip pairing a sound onset to the frame where damage becomes possible — event-timeline.json has ticks and the waveforms have seconds, but nothing renders the two together, so 'does the audio peak land on the tick the trace says damage becomes possible' is unanswerable from these fifteen files. Fix: add a strip that overlays the master-out envelope on tick gridlines with the damage-window ticks marked, for one light swing, one heavy swing and one enemy attack. Everything needed is already in event-timeline.json and envelopes.json.

biggest_gap.element: The brute's 20-tick wind-up and its commit peak (ticks 129-148, brute-only seed 1, strip.png + strip-fullspan.png). Measured on the strip cells (true cell pitch 340x286): the brute's BODY is pixel-static for the whole wind-up - all anticipation is carried by the hammer prop rotating ~60 degrees, and the sprite's orange bbox top oscillates between screen y=38 and y=42 (2 source px, net travel zero). No lean, no squash, no scale, no shadow change. Whole-frame change per 2 ticks bottoms out at 0.11% of pixels with |dL|>8 (t=139->141) - a frozen frame in the middle of the tell. The ground danger mark is a 3-step staircase, not a ramp: its p99 is pinned at exactly 207.3 and max at 208.0 for ticks 129-141 (13 ticks / 217 ms of literally zero change), steps once to p99 238.1 at t=143, holds flat for 6 more ticks, then steps to 239.6 at release. And the commit flash (sprite orange 300 -> 580 px, +93%) fires at t=145 and is already decaying at t=147, fully gone by the release at 149 - 11 ticks / 183 ms BEFORE damage lands at 156 (trace: enemyWindup 129, enemyAttack 149, playerHurt 156). The loudest frame of the telegraph is not the damage frame; it leads it by 183 ms and has decayed to nothing by then.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-density-02 the incoming danger is one continuously EXTENDING high-value path: it draws itself across the floor tick by tick, so the player reads time-to-arrival from how far it has drawn - the tell encodes when, not just where. Its brightest pixels sit at p99 252.7 against a frame median of 22.6 (11x the background) and are the only bright thing in frame. ref-density-01 does the same for impact: white 255 over a median of 21. In both, the hazard is separated from everything else by VALUE and by continuous growth, never by a small hue shift on a 16px body, and the peak is at the moment of consequence.
biggest_gap.fix: Drive the entire 27-tick window (129 -> 156) from one 0->1 progress value and ramp three channels continuously off it, with the peak landing on tick 156, not 145. (a) Body kinematics: lean/squash the brute at least 4 source px monotonically over 129-148, then extend through 149-156, so the silhouette itself counts down - no oscillation, no reversal. (b) Ground mark: ramp rim luminance and radius every tick instead of stepping at 143, and let its brightest value arrive at 156 as the brightest thing in the frame; draw the rim so the player standing inside it does not occlude it. (c) Hold the commit flash through the release instead of decaying it at 147, so the loudest frame and the damage tick are the same frame. Success test: no two consecutive sampled frames in 129-156 are within 1% changed pixels, and argmax(frame p99) == 156.

other_gaps: PEAK VALUE / CONTACT. Element: the hit VFX at t=156-159. Frame max luminance is 239.6 on ALL twelve fullspan frames - wind-up, release, hit-stop, recovery, idle. The hammer landing does not produce one pixel brighter than the quiet room already contains; it only moves p99 236.7 -> 239.6 (+2.9 of 255) and pct>230 from ~1.01% to 2.48%. The palette ceiling itself sits 15 code values below 255. Stronger: refs hold their only 255s in the impact (ref-density-01 p99 203 over median 21; ref-density-02 p99 252.7 over median 22.6). Fix: reserve the band >=245 exclusively for contact and telegraph peaks and let nothing static exceed ~225, so the impact has somewhere to be brighter than. (Phrased in the brute's terms; the room's ambient share of the range is the arena lane's assigned item.)

CAMERA. Element: impact shake. Best-fit integer shift of static wall geometry vs frame 00 is dx=0 dy=0 with err<0.70 on 11 of 12 frames; only the hit-stop frame t=159 fits better at dx=-2 screen px = -1 SOURCE px, dy=0. So the heaviest blow in the game buys at most one source pixel of camera motion, and it is HORIZONTAL against an attack whose event angle is 1.5708 rad - straight down. Fix: shake along the blow's axis (vertical here), amplitude >=2 source px on the first freeze tick decaying to 0 across the 4-tick freeze. Compute the amplitude in source pixels; anything under 1 px is not a subtle shake, it is no shake.

PUNISH WINDOW IS MUTE. Element: the brute's 34-tick / 567 ms recover state (t=164-198). Consecutive change across it is 4.30, 3.52, 2.98, 1.65, 2.44 % of pixels; the pair t=183->189 (1.65%, meanabs 1.53) is the quietest in the entire capture and sits at the centre of the window. Frame p99 returns to exactly 236.7 and pct>230 to 1.009% - identical to the pre-attack idle. The state that means 'hit me now for 567 ms' is photometrically indistinguishable from the state that means 'I am about to kill you'. Fix: a dedicated recover read that persists all 34 ticks and visibly DECAYS as the window closes - hammer head embedded in the floor plus a rim or steam that shrinks tick by tick - so the closing of the window is legible without reading a HUD.

KNOCKBACK ENDS IN SUB-PIXEL DRIFT. Element: player recovery after playerHurt at t=156. Player y goes 184.0 -> 186.6 -> 191.4 -> 194.1 -> 195.3 -> 195.8 -> 196.1 -> 196.2. After render-tick 173 the player travels 0.9 px in 18 ticks = 0.05 px/tick over 300 ms - under one source pixel, invisible motion occupying half the recovery. And the curve is a pure monotone decay: it never overshoots past the settle point and returns. Against the acceptance criterion we have neither overshoot nor snap; we have a creep. Fix: finish the knockback in ~12 ticks with a 2-3 source px overshoot and a 2-tick return, and round render positions to whole source pixels so no motion budget is spent below the pixel.

HIT-STOP LENGTH. Element: hitStopFreezeTicksOnContact = 4 (67 ms) for the game's heaviest single blow (1 of 5 HP, 12.2 px of knockback), with no companion scale or flash hold. Long enough to see, but it does not read as a weight class. Fix: 6-8 ticks for the brute specifically, differentiated from a light hit, so the player can feel the weight through the freeze alone.

DENSITY. Element: events per second in a combat frame. Ours carries 4 discrete moving elements (brute, player, ground mark, dust puff), 1 of which is a hazard; median inter-frame change 2.4% of pixels with one pair at 0.11%. ref-density-01 holds roughly 35 discrete elements in one still - a boss, 4 enemies, ~8 hazard projectiles, 2 tracer paths, a 3-lobe smoke plume, ~12 debris motes, 3 pickups, 4 dropped guns - and still reads because they are value-sorted (hazards 200-255, actors mid, floor <25). Fix: add CONSEQUENCE-bearing elements, not confetti - an impact shockwave ring, debris ejected along the blow's axis, a floor crack decal that persists into the punish window - each keyed to the tick schedule so the added density is information. Do not adopt the reference's bullet-hell composition; our read must stay one-hazard-at-a-time.

COMPOSITION / AXIS COLLAPSE. Element: the encounter geometry. Brute (208, 158.4), player (208, 184), the ground mark, the gold mandala's centre and the doorway all sit on the same vertical line x=208, nested concentrically - five collinear elements. The refs are consistently off-axis: ref-density-01 puts the boss upper-right and the player lower-left with the action on the diagonal; ref-density-03 centres the actors but breaks the mirror with unequal furniture. Fix (brute-owned, not the arena's mirrored room): give the lunge a lateral component and offset the ground mark from the brute's centre by the lunge vector, so the mark says which way to dodge and the fight stops resolving on the room's mirror axis.

VOCABULARY COLLISION. Element: the commit tell and the damage feedback use the same channel - a full-sprite colour wash on a 16px body (brute goes orange at t=145, player goes white-blown at t=159), 11 ticks apart, meaning two different things. Fix: reserve full-sprite tint for damage taken; make the commit tell a shape and value event (silhouette change plus rim), so the two never compete.

AXIS SCORES THIS ROUND (0-5): 1 Readability 2 - the frame says 'brute, hammer up, mark on floor' but never says WHEN, and at t=147 the mark is occluded by the player standing in it. 2 Material and light 2 - the R1 palette repair is real and visible (p99 239.6, mid-tones open, no crush), but there is no hierarchy: frame max is 239.6 in every single frame and the floor (meanL ~148) outshines both actors (brute box meanL 125.6-132.1). 3 Feel chain 2 - anticipation present but 2 source px and prop-only; exactly one readable contact frame (t=159, pct>230 2.48% vs 1.01% baseline) which passes; freeze 4 ticks is short but visible; recovery neither overshoots nor snaps; visual peak leads damage by 11 ticks. 4 Composition 1 - five elements collinear inside a concentric ring. 5 Pixel integrity 3 - uniform 16px scale, integer zoom, static geometry pixel-identical frame to frame (best-fit dx=dy=0, err<0.70, so no shimmer); docked for the free-rotating hammer prop resampling off-grid every frame while every other sprite is grid-locked, and for sub-pixel entity positions (y=158.4, 173.6, 176.3, 196.2). 6 Density 1. 7 Originality 3 - not a copy: gold/grey mandala hall against the refs' near-black blue, melee-first, one-hazard read rather than bullet-hell. Held back by under-commitment, not imitation - the room's decor is currently more distinctive than anything the fight does.

biggest_gap.element: The brute's slam ends INSIDE the player and parks there for the whole punish window. Trace (strip-fullspan.png.json): brute y 158.4 -> 173.6 (t153) -> 176.3 (t159) -> 176.1, then frozen at 176.1 for all 34 recover ticks (t164-198). Player y 184 -> 196.2. Final separation 10-20 px with two sprites drawn ~20 px tall, so from t=153 to t=198 (45 ticks, 0.75 s) the two silhouettes interpenetrate. In the enlarged actor grid the recover frames (t=165,171,177,183,189,195) are a single unreadable jumble: the brute's grey hammer sits on the player's grey helmet, its brown body wraps the player's shield, and there is no floor pixel between them. The punish window - the one thing a 27-tick telegraph exists to buy you - is the least legible stretch in the piece, and the brute is also motionless through it (y unchanged to 0.1 px for 34 ticks), so the frame is visually static for 0.57 s.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In all three reference frames no two actors ever share pixels. ref-density-01: the red boss and the four eyeball enemies each sit on a discrete hard-edged dark ellipse with clear floor between every pair. ref-density-03: the boss is a full body-length from the player and casts a hard shadow; the threat between them is a green beam, not a body. The hard elliptical drop shadow is the specific device that keeps silhouettes separable when things do get close, and the attack's reach - not the attacker's body - is what crosses the gap.
biggest_gap.fix: Two changes, both verifiable from the trace. (1) End the slam one body-radius short: cap the brute's attack travel so it plants at y ~= 166-168 against a player at 184, and add a separation push on contact so the pair never re-close during recover. Acceptance: no tick in 149-198 where the sprite boxes overlap more than ~25%. (2) Give the brute and the player each a hard 2 px-tall elliptical drop shadow (flat colour, no soft ramp, pinned to the 1x pixel grid) so any residual overlap still reads as two bodies at two floor depths. Then re-shoot the fullspan strip and confirm the recover frames show two separable silhouettes.

(a) Anticipation distinguishable from idle: YES but late - the ground mark appears at t=129 and the brute's body tint fires at t=147, i.e. only the last 6 of 27 tell ticks carry a pose/colour change; frames t=129/135/141 are near-identical raised-hammer poses.
