CAPTURE GAP that blocks two acceptance criteria. Element: the protocol strip (every-2) runs t=129-151 and stops 5 ticks BEFORE first damage at t=156; the fullspan strip (every-6) samples t=153 and t=159 and skips 154-158. So the damage tick 156 and the whole active window 156-160 appear in zero submitted images. Stronger does: n/a (stills), but the round's own acceptance criteria demand a per-tick view of contact. Fix: add a third strip, every-1, t=152-166, 15 frames - it covers release-to-damage, the hit-stop, and the first recover ticks in one image. Without it 'exactly one contact frame' and 'peak on the damage tick' are unfalsifiable.

KNOCKBACK IS A SLIDE, NOT A PUNCH. Element: player y after the hit - 184.0 (t147), 186.6 (t159), 191.4 (t165), 194.1 (t171), 195.3 (t177), 195.8 (t183), 196.1 (t189), 196.2 (t195). Total 12.2 px, but only 2.6 px arrive during the 4-tick hit-stop; 9.6 px (78%) arrive AFTER the freeze ends, spread over ticks 160-183, and the curve is a pure exponential decay with no overshoot and no counter-settle. It creeps for ~27 ticks, longer than the entire 20-tick windup. Stronger does: reference impacts are delivered as displacement, then a stop - the actor is somewhere else by the next frame, not drifting. Fix: front-load it - ~9 px in the first 4-6 ticks with a hard ease-out, one 1-px counter-move at ticks 8-10, fully settled by tick 12. Acceptance: >=70% of the displacement inside the first 6 ticks and a visible 1-px reversal before rest.

NO CAMERA RESPONSE ON THE HIT. Element: measured the floor/wall horizontal edge position per frame in a column clear of both actors - it sits at cell y 143 and 157 in EVERY frame including t=159, the frozen contact-adjacent tick, identical to t=129. Zero displacement, not a subtle shake. (Caveat: only one contact-adjacent tick is captured; the every-1 strip above would settle it.) Stronger does: a hammer slam that costs 20% of your HP is the archetypal case for a camera kick. Fix: compute the amplitude, do not eyeball it - at 480x270 anything under ~1 whole game px is nothing. Use 2 px on the slam axis at tick 156, decaying to 0 by tick 162, integer-quantised so the pixel grid never breaks.

THE TELL'S ESCALATION IS A TEXTURE SWAP, NOT A RAMP. Element: mean luminance of the ground-mark band minus the equivalent bare-floor band to its left, per tick: -12.3 (t129), -26.8 (t131), -29.0 (t137-141), then -23.2 (t143, the commit lock), -23.9 (t147), -31.3 (t149). The mark gets LESS different from the floor at the exact tick the attack commits, because the escalation swaps a dark stipple for a stipple-plus-white-rim instead of intensifying. At a glance t=141 and t=147 look equally dangerous. The mark is also only ~11% of range darker than the floor, low chroma, and drawn UNDER the player who is standing in it. Stronger does: ref-density-02's red/yellow bullet paths and ref-density-03's green beam are the highest-chroma things in frame and are drawn over everything - the danger signal never competes with the floor's own value. Fix: draw the mark above the actors, hold one hue that is not in the room's tan/grey palette, and make the escalation monotonic in one channel (rim width 1 -> 2 -> 3 px, or alpha 0.4 -> 0.7 -> 1.0). Acceptance: contrast-against-floor increases at every 2-tick sample from t=129 to t=149, with no dip.

IMPACT BURST IS DIRECTIONLESS AND SOFT-CENTRED. Element: at t=159 the contact VFX is a radially symmetric dotted ring plus a pale blue-white lobe with a many-step interior ramp, centred on the brute. Nothing in it says the hammer came straight DOWN, and it fully occludes both actors rather than reading over them. Stronger does: ref-density-01's explosion is directional - hard chunky grey smoke puffs and pink streaks thrown along the shot vector, a small white core, a saturated white->yellow->orange ramp in 3-4 steps, and the actors' silhouettes survive underneath it. Fix: flatten the ring to a 2:1 ellipse on the ground plane, throw 4-6 hard-edged 2x2 debris pixels along the slam vector, cut the interior ramp to 3 palette steps with one genuinely white core cluster, and draw the brute's dark outline back on top of the burst.

COMPOSITION IS A PERFECT MIRROR. Element: brute x=208, player x=208, ground mark centred on x=208, and a large set of concentric rings centred on the same axis directly behind them - the frame folds onto itself down the middle, and every element is grid-snapped to that one axis. Stronger does: ref-density-01 pushes the boss up-right and the player low-left with two diagonal tracers cutting the frame; ref-density-03 offsets the boss high and the player low with the beam as the only connecting diagonal. Asymmetry with intent, in both. Fix: have the brute commit from an angle rather than straight down the column (approach offset of 20-30 px before the windup lock), and stop centring the arena's ring motif on the fight's own axis.

DENSITY, flagged as scenario-limited rather than scored as a straight loss. Element: between consecutive 2-tick samples ~11-13% of the crop's pixels change, and the diff map shows most of that is the animated background rings and the pulsing HUD hint row, not the fight - the fight itself is two actors, one ground mark and one dust puff. Stronger does: ref-density-02 carries ~40 discrete bullets on four sinuous paths plus two enemies in one frame. Fix: not a brute-lane fix at this scenario size; note it and re-measure density on a full-wave capture rather than a brute-only crop, otherwise this axis will read 1 forever for reasons that have nothing to do with the brute.

biggest_gap.element: The contact flash at tick 156 (exhibit-impact.png, the frame the trace calls firstDamage/playerHurt). Measured in game pixels: a 46x36 cream disc, 687 px, 6.7% of the 128x80 view, built from three near-identical flat tones (236,189,153) / (236,197,183) / (236,204,203) — a 14-unit luminance range from edge to centre, peaking at 210.7/255 with 0.00% of the frame above 229. It is ~3x the brute's own 14 px body width and it fully occludes BOTH fighters: only the brute's crown row and one 4 px white block escape it. At the single tick damage lands you cannot see who hit whom or where either body is.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: ref-density-01's explosion core is ~22x17 game px, about a quarter of the boss's 82 px width, and ramps 255-white through yellow and orange to dark red across that short span; the frame hits a true 255 with 0.53% of pixels above 229. The boss's face and silhouette read straight through the blast. The size and energy are carried OUTWARD by directional smoke plumes, spark trails and tracer lines that point away from contact — never by an opaque area parked on top of the actors. Contact is a small hot point plus direction, not a large flat pancake.
biggest_gap.fix: Invert the flash's mass distribution. Shrink the opaque core to ~10-14 game px and move it to the actual contact point between axe and player rather than centring it on the brute's feet. Give it a real ramp instead of a 14-unit one: clamp the centre to the authored white end and step hard through yellow and orange into the existing dark ring in 3-4 steps. Spend the reclaimed ~500 px of area on 6-10 directional streak/debris pixels thrown outward along the swing vector. Acceptance: both silhouettes remain readable in the peak frame, and the frame reaches the authored white end.

other_gaps: Two contact frames, not one (axis 1, axis 3). The lunge disc goes solid full-bright orange at t≈150-155 — 34.1% of the panel changes between t=147 and t=153 — and then the cream flash fires at t=156-159. Same centre, same warm hue family, same filled-ellipse shape, three ticks apart. Nothing tells 'the attack is now live' apart from 'you were hit'. Fix: split the shape language. Keep the active window as an unfilled outline or arc, and make contact the only filled, only white-cored, only debris-throwing event in the cycle.

567 ms of punish window with no event (axis 3, axis 6). Trace: recovery runs 164-198, 34 ticks. Sampled panels t=165..195 change 6.05 / 28.66 / 5.49 / 5.58 / 6.12 percent — one positional shift, then a static hunch. The trace also records the ground mark gone from t=171 on, so ~24 of the 34 punish ticks carry the pose and nothing else. Acceptance asks recovery to overshoot and settle; this snaps to a hold. Fix: an overshoot past the settle pose in the first ~8 ticks, then a decaying vulnerability mark (dimming ring, wobble, dropped-guard silhouette) that visibly counts the window down for the player.

Impact camera kick is one game pixel on one axis (axis 3). Computed, not eyeballed: over a 136x60 background sample every frame is an exact integer translation of the last (mean abs err 0.00-0.01); the camera pans +1 screen px per 6 ticks at x2 throughout, and at t=159 it reads -1 instead of the trend's +1. Net displacement: 1 game px horizontal, 0 vertical, partly cancelled by the pan running the other way. At 480x270 that is nearly no shake. Fix: kick 2-3 game px along the swing vector with a 2-tick return, and freeze the follow-pan for the duration of hitstop so the kick is not competing with it.

The event never owns the top of the range (axis 2). Scoped to the flash's own ceiling, not the room's floor. At t=156 the flash peaks at 210.7 while the brute's STATIC steel axe blade reads 239.6 in the same crop, and the impact adds only +0.6 percentage points of pixels above 183 over the windup frame (1.62% vs 1.04%). All three reference frames reach 255. Fix: let the flash clamp to the authored white end for its first 2 ticks so contact is the brightest thing on screen for exactly as long as the freeze lasts.

Player-hurt spawns no particles; enemy-hurt does (axis 6, axis 1). poses.png brute-stagger throws a cluster of pink debris pixels plus a hit ring when the ENEMY is hit. exhibit-impact.png at playerHurt throws none — no debris, no floor dust, no spark. The two halves of the exchange speak different vocabularies, so damage direction is not legible from the frame. Fix: give player-hurt its own debris burst in a cool desaturated hue, so hue alone tells the player which way damage went.

Density at the loudest tick (axis 6). The peak damage frame contains exactly two transient elements: one cream disc and one dithered ring. ref-density-01 carries roughly 40 simultaneous transients at its loudest moment (tracers, shell casings, smoke plumes, sparks, blood specks, pickup hearts, muzzle flash). Fix: raise the count from state the sim already has — floor dust off the lunge, chips knocked from the ground mark, an axe trail, a knockback drag streak. Do NOT close this by importing Gungeon's confetti; axis 7 is currently a 4 and copying the reference's composition would be a regression, not progress.

biggest_gap.element: The contact frame itself — exhibit-impact.png at t=156, the exact tick the trace fires playerHurt. The hit is one opaque, flat, cream-orange ellipse centred on the actors. Measured on the 128x80 game frame: 809 game px above L 0.55, 604 above L 0.70, and ZERO pixels above L 0.85. Brightest pixel in the whole frame is RGB 236,204,203 (L=0.826) — nothing reaches white. The blob erases the brute down to the crown row and swallows the player entirely; at the one moment the player must read who hit whom and which way they are being thrown, the frame contains no silhouette, no outline, no direction vector.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: All three reference frames build the same event as a value pyramid with a hard apex and an intact silhouette. Measured identically: ref-01 0.28% of frame at L>0.95 / 0.79% >0.85 / 1.53% >0.70; ref-02 1.50 / 2.98 / 4.29; ref-03 0.69 / 2.37 / 5.90. Every one touches 255,255,255, and 7-18% of the bright mass sits in the top apex band. The core is tiny (ref-01's is roughly 12x14 game px), and it is layered — white core, yellow ring, saturated orange, red rim, grey smoke plumes on independent arcs — sitting ON TOP of the boss while the boss's face, eyes, mouth and dark outline stay fully legible underneath. The flash adds light; it never subtracts the character.
biggest_gap.fix: Invert the area/intensity trade: shrink the flash footprint by roughly 4-6x (target under 150 game px above L 0.55) and give it a real apex — a 6-10 game px core clamped to the palette's authored white so the frame finally has pixels above L 0.95, then two banded falloff steps (hot core, mid, rim) rather than one fill. Draw it additively over the actors and re-stamp the brute's and player's outline pixels on top afterwards so neither silhouette can ever be erased, and offset the whole thing along the attack angle (1.5708, straight south) instead of centring it, so contact carries direction.

FEEL-CHAIN, criterion 2 — exactly ONE readable contact frame. Element: the peak is a plateau, not a frame. The effect is at full strength across t=153 (solid opaque orange disc), t=156 (cream blob), and t=159 (blob + dotted ring), and a dark ring remnant still sits on the floor at t=165; it is gone by t=171. That is ~15-18 ticks / 250-300 ms of continuous bloom against a 4-tick hitstop — the effect outlives the freeze by ~11 ticks, so it stops saying 'this is the moment' and becomes ambient lighting. The references concentrate the same energy into a core that reads as one instant. Fix: cut total effect lifetime to 6-8 ticks with a hard 2-tick peak and an immediate step-down, so the visual apex and the 4-tick freeze end together.

FEEL-CHAIN, criterion 4 — recovery overshoot and settle. Element: the brute does not settle, it snaps. Enemy y from the trace: 158.4 -> 166.4 -> 173.6 -> 176.3, then 176.1 held to within 0.2 px for all 34 ticks of recover (t=165,171,177,183,189,195 all read 176.1). No recoil, no drift back, no easing. Note the player knockback in the same trace DOES decay correctly (184 -> 184.4 -> 186.6 -> 191.4 -> 194.1 -> 195.3 -> 195.8 -> 196.1 -> 196.2), which proves the settle curve exists in the codebase and is simply not applied to the attacker. Fix: give the brute a 3-4 px recoil back along the lunge axis over ~6 ticks with the same decay the player already uses.

The 34-tick / 567 ms punish window is visually silent, and its back half actively lies. Element: from t=165 to t=195 the only recovery signal is the brute's pose — no ground mark (it has faded by 171), no tint, no lingering flash. Worse, by t=189 and t=195 the axe is back overhead, which is the same silhouette read as the windup at t=129-147. The player cannot tell 'safe to punish' from 'about to be hit' during the single most important window in the fight. Fix: hold the axe DOWN for the whole recover state so the raised-axe silhouette is reserved exclusively for windup, and add a persistent low-value recovery cue that decays across the full 34 ticks (a dim ground ring or a desaturated body tint) so the window has a visible clock.

Zero secondary particles at contact. Element: the hit emits exactly one radial blob and nothing else — no discrete debris, no sparks, no smoke, no spatter, no shell or chip on an independent arc. Stronger: every reference throws 6+ independently-arcing elements from a single hit — ref-01 alone has grey smoke plumes on three separate trajectories, red spatter dots, a shell, and ring pickups scattering. Fix: emit 5-8 pooled 1-2 px particles at contact on a 120-degree spread centred on the attack angle, each with its own decay, so the impact has parts that move differently rather than one thing that scales.

The whole attack is one hue family, so nothing separates a warning from a wound. Element: telegraph, lunge disc, and contact flash all live between 236,162,110 and 236,204,203 — the impact is just a paler version of the telegraph. Stronger: the references break hue AND value between phases — a red-orange ground/rim against a white-yellow core, with dark smoke providing a hard negative-value anchor next to the highlight. The windup fan at t=129 IS directional and reads well — that quality is then thrown away as the mark fills in. EVIDENCE GAP, blocking two acceptance criteria. biggest_gap.element: The live bolt is quieter than its own warning. In the bolt lane (world y 112–130) across the 24-tick aim window t=65–71, the magenta telegraph measures 98–100 native px spanning ~100 px of x-extent. The moment the bolt actually exists and can kill you, t=74–80, magenta in that same lane collapses to 12–34 native px spanning 13–20 px. biggest_gap.stronger_does: In B the live projectile is always the loudest thing in its neighbourhood and the telegraph is the thin one. ref-density-02: each white bullet core is 52–70 native px (8x8 to 9x14) with 8+ on screen at once, while the telegraphed red laser web that fills 16.3% of the frame is drawn as a 2–3 px line that never outshouts a bullet. ref-density-03: one live laser is a 4,982 native-px element with a 1,135 px head crossing the room, white-yellow core inside a green halo. Warning thin, threat fat — the exact inverse of ours.
biggest_gap.fix: Invert the hierarchy in the caster's render. Cap the aim telegraph at roughly 30 native px in-lane (thin it as the charge completes rather than thickening it), and give the bolt a body: a 3–4 px white core, a 6–8 px saturated halo, and a 20–30 px tail that persists 3–4 ticks behind the head. Acceptance test, computable from the same strip: in the y 112–130 band, cell t=74 must carry at least 2x the L>0.72 pixel count of cell t=59, and in-lane magenta at t=74–80 must exceed 120 native px — above, not below, the telegraph's 100.

Axis 2 moved up this wave: the R1 grade fix landed and is measurable — our cut frame now sits at p99 239.6 and 4.43% of pixels above 72% luminance, inside the reference band of 4.71 / 4.02 / 5.43%. Axis 6 is the one dragging the piece.

The capture ends before the thing it is meant to prove. strip.png's last cell is t=83 with 'FREEZE 2' still on the clock — two ticks INSIDE the hitstop. There is no post-freeze frame anywhere in this round's evidence, so 'does recovery overshoot and settle rather than snap' cannot be answered at all. Stronger practice: sample past the event's tail. The discharge is smaller than the room's decoration. At t=74 the muzzle flash core is a 47 native-px blob in an 11x9 bbox; the row of five torch icons above the knight are 30 px each at the identical peak luminance. Total event chroma at the fire tick is 108 native px, 1.12% of the frame. B's ref-density-01 puts a 250 native-px core in the same kind of moment with 88 satellite spark blobs inside a matched 120x80 window. Fix: a 3-frame flash starting at a 10–14 px core and decaying, plus 4–6 ejected sparks thrown back along the firing axis, plus a 1–2 px recoil kick of the caster sprite — there is currently zero recoil, the caster's x is 163.0 at t=68 and still exactly 163.0 at t=74.

The cut — the caster piece's entire reason to exist — has no burst of its own. At t=81 the boltCut point measures 20 bright native px and 55 magenta px total, sitting behind the player's sword arc at 285 px in a 31x23 bbox. The player's action is 5x louder than the outcome it caused, so the frame teaches 'the sword did something', not 'you cut the bolt'. B's ref-density-02 impact carries 1,140 bright px across 166 blobs in a matched 120x80 window, with a 481 px core. Fix: on boltCut emit a radial burst in the bolt's own hue at the cut point — 8–12 shards thrown along the bolt axis plus a 12–16 px ring for 3–4 ticks — sized so the cut point beats the sword arc in SATURATED pixels while the arc keeps the white.

Hue carries no information because the caster owns exactly one. Robe, aim line, bolt, muzzle flash and stagger flash are all the same magenta. Our cut frame measures mean saturation 0.131 with 1.35% of pixels above sat 0.5; B measures 0.445/33.3%, 0.588/60.2% and 0.279/19.4%. B separates meaning by hue inside a single frame — ref-density-02 runs red for the persistent hazard, cyan for lightning, white for live bullets, orange for fire. Fix, and this part needs nothing from the arena lane: split the caster's palette three ways — cool violet for the telegraph, a hotter white-core-to-orange for the live bolt, a third for the stagger flash.

Light is spent in two big lumps instead of many small ones. The cut frame's 425 bright pixels sit in 28 blobs and 76% of them are in just two (213 + 110, both sword arc). Matched 120x80 windows in B: 89 blobs (ref-01) and 166 blobs (ref-02) at the same or higher bright budget. B looks busy without looking brighter because the same light is divided across shells, embers, debris and sparks. Fix: every caster event should spawn 6–12 short-lived 1–2 px particles rather than one larger sprite.

No headroom above the room. Every hot pixel in both exhibit frames clamps to exactly 239.6 — the muzzle flash, the sword arc, the torch icons and the caster's robe highlight are the identical value, so nothing in this game can ever be hotter than a wall torch. B reaches 255 and reserves it: ref-01 p99 203.4 with only 0.23% of pixels at 250+, ref-03 p99 235.6 with 0.35%. Fix: pull static props down one authored step and reserve the top ~5% of the ramp for event cores only. (Distinct from the assigned arena item, which is about how MANY pixels sit above 72%; this is about there being no rung above the room's own lights.)

poses.png is unusable as evidence and was unusable last round too (self-reported in timing.json, still shipped). A judge cannot compare three tiles that disagree on lighting and UI. Fix in tools/poses.ts: render on the tick each pose names rather than once at the end of stepping, and pin lighting and HUD state across all tiles.

Checked and NOT a gap, recorded so it is not re-raised: camera drift. Cross-correlating the static wall band of every strip cell against cell 00 gives a maximum shift of 1 native px across all 12 frames. The background is stable; what reads as movement is caster 2's telegraph sweeping through the crop.

biggest_gap.element: The event flash itself — the caster's discharge at t=74 (exhibit-fire.png) and the contact flash at t=81 (exhibit.png). Measured at game resolution: our discharge is 86 bright pixels (L>150) inside a 26x11 px bbox, built from exactly two tones — a core of (236,240,246) and a ring of (236,135,245) — arranged as a bilaterally symmetric 4-point star, with zero embers thrown clear, zero smoke, and a core that peaks at 239.6 luminance. Nothing in either of our frames exceeds 239.6, and 239.6 is the same tone the quiet wall highlight already uses: peak-white pixel count is 224 at t=68 (mid-windup, nothing happening), 136 at t=74 (the discharge) and 116 at t=83 (the hit). The event does not own the top of the frame — it does not even match the windup.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: Exhibit A renders at the same 480x270 native grid (measured: 4px blocks in ref-density-01), so this is like for like. Its impact flash is 447 bright px, a four-band hard ramp — 255-white core (122 px above 240 luminance), then yellow, then orange, then deep red, each band 4-8 game px wide with a hard step between them — inside a spiky, irregular, non-symmetric silhouette. Around it sit ~20 separate ember pixels thrown clear of the blob with black gaps between them, and a 2-tone grey smoke puff that outlives the flash. Its quiet room, by contrast, tops out at 181 luminance: the reference reserves ~74 points of headroom that only an event is allowed to touch.
biggest_gap.fix: Rebuild the discharge and contact flashes as layered pixel shapes rather than a core plus a ring. (1) Reserve pure 255 white for event cores only and let the flash reach it — our clamp at the palette's 239.6 top tone means the flash can never outshine a wall. (2) Step out from that core through 3-4 hard authored bands (white -> hot magenta -> violet -> dark violet for the caster; white -> pale gold -> steel for the sword contact), each band at least 2 game px thick, no alpha ramp between them. (3) Break the silhouette: spike lengths should vary per fire so no two discharges are the same shape, and never mirror left/right. (4) Add 8-16 ember pixels ejected with real velocity that outlive the flash by 6-10 ticks, and a 2-tone smoke puff at the staff tip. (5) Scale the whole footprint to roughly 3x the current bbox — target ~250-450 bright px at the peak instead of 86. This is not the arena-lighting item: in a pitch-black room our flash would still be 86 px of two tones.

AXIS SCORES 0-5 this round: 1 Readability 3 | 2 Material and light 2 | 3 Feel chain 3 | 4 Composition 2 | 5 Pixel integrity 4 | 6 Density 1 | 7 Originality 4.

Knockback points the wrong way. On the damage tick the caster moves from x=163.0 to x=166.8 (+3.8 px, toward the player) while the player lunges from 208.1 to 200.3 (-7.8 px, into the caster): the two sprites converge 11.6 px at the moment of contact, which is the opposite of the separation that sells an impact. The trace shows why: the swing event carries angle pi, but the hit event it produced carries angle 0 — the bolt's heading, not the sword's. Fix: drive the impulse from the swing angle so the struck enemy is pushed away, and hold the lunge until after the freeze so contact reads as a shove, not a merge.

The slash ribbon is a different material from everything it overlaps. 481 arc pixels at game resolution span 102 distinct luminances (roughly one new tone every 4.7 px — a continuous alpha ramp), with soft rounded ends and no outline. A 40x20 wall patch beside it uses 9 colours total and every sprite carries a 1px dark outline. Fix: quantize the arc to 3-4 authored tones with hard steps, give it a 1px dark edge like the sprites, and cut the ends square.

The bolt in flight has no danger signature. It is a ~15x2 world-px magenta lance moving 1.83 px/tick (110 px/s) with no trail, no glow and no persistence, and it is the same magenta family as the harmless dashed aim telegraph that crosses the same frames (caster 2's line). Exhibit A never lets that confusion exist: every live projectile has a hard bright core plus a trail 40+ px long (ref-01) or a core-and-halo beam (ref-03), and the danger lines in ref-02 are the single largest graphic on screen. Fix: give the bolt a 255-white head, a 3-4 px trail that persists 4-6 ticks, and a hue reserved for live danger that the telegraph is never allowed to use.

Anticipation is back-loaded. Across the 24-tick aim window, the caster's charge box changes by under 3 mean-abs per 2 ticks from t=52 to t=64 — half the telegraph is a standing wizard plus a short dotted line, with no orb at all. The orb and the body tint only appear at t=66 and grow to t=72. Fix: start the orb at aim tick 0 and grow it monotonically across the full window, or shorten the aim to the 10 ticks that actually read.

Contact is ambiguous between two mechanics. boltCut at x=184.8 and the sword hit on the caster at x=163 resolve on the same tick, 22 px apart, sharing one white arc and one freeze. Nothing on screen tells you whether you cut the bolt or hit the wizard, and nothing connects the cut point to the damage 22 px away. Fix: separate them by a few ticks, or give the cut its own local VFX — a spark at the cut point and the bolt's two halves scattering — so cause and effect are visibly distinct.

The hero frame crops its own subject out. exhibit.png uses crop x=172 while the caster being hit sits at x=166.8 — the target of the round is half off-frame at the left edge, and the hit sparks (~19 warm px) are cut by the border. Both reference stills centre their event. Fix: crop on the midpoint of attacker and target, not on the player.

Composition is collinear. Player, caster and bolt all sit on y=121, so the whole event resolves along one horizontal line through the middle of a symmetric brick field, with a near-black floor below. ref-03 stages its beam on a diagonal across a lit, asymmetrically dressed floor. Fix: offset the caster in y so the telegraph, the bolt and the swing form a triangle rather than a rule.

Density is an order of magnitude down. Our contact frame carries about 6 discrete moving elements (player, caster, arc, bolt puff, spark cluster, HUD hearts). ref-density-01 carries 40+ (bullets, casings, embers, three smoke plumes, five enemies, pickups, two long trails). Even discounting that this is a 1v1 probe, nothing in our frame decays, scatters or lingers — every element is born and dies within its own tick.

Camera kick exists and is not sub-pixel — computed, not eyeballed: the background shifts ~2 world px between t=80 and t=83 (best-match rigid shift on two separate wall patches, residual well above the 0.0-0.07 of the static frames). But the capture ends at t=83 with 2 freeze ticks still to run, so whether it overshoots and settles or snaps back cannot be judged. Fix: extend the strip 12-15 ticks past the end of the freeze and label the settle.

Evidence integrity, which cost this round real information: poses.png's bolt-flight tile shows no bolt at all (empty floor), its three tiles sit in three different lighting states, and only one of them carries the AIM/STRIKE prompt overlay; strip-every2.png — the protocol-literal capture — ends at t=72, two ticks before the bolt is fired, so it contains no event whatsoever. And there is no audio artifact anywhere in the round, so the input-produces-no-sound check could not be run at all.

biggest_gap.element: The caster bolt between fire and cut (t=74 to t=81) in strip.png / strip-every2.png. Measured at native scale, the bolt's leading edge is at x=81 at t=74, still x=81 at t=76, still x=81 at t=78, and x=85 at t=80 - it does not move for 6 of the projectile's 7 ticks of life. Meanwhile its tail grows BACKWARDS through the emitter: the streak's rear edge runs 60 -> 51 -> 49 -> 53. The streak body is 33 px long; the trace says the bolt travels 12.8 world px total (172 -> 184.83 in 7 ticks, 110 px/s). The trail is 2.6x longer than the entire flight, and the t=74 muzzle burst already reaches 20 px downrange, so the flash overshoots the whole flight path and nothing ever appears to leave the caster. It reads as a lamp switching on at the shooter's hand, not as a thing coming at you.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-density-01 and ref-density-03 every live projectile is clear of its muzzle in the frame it appears in: the yellow tracers cross the full frame, the green beam runs the entire gap between shooter and target, and the trail length is a function of distance covered, so a single still tells you the direction and the speed of the threat. The flash never reaches further downrange than the bullet.
biggest_gap.fix: Split the one effect into three and let distance drive the art. (1) Muzzle burst: clip it to a forward cone about 10 px long by 8 px tall, anchored at the aim muzzle offset, dead in 2 ticks - it must never reach further than the bolt's position at that tick. (2) Head: a small hard 6-8 px sprite whose per-tick displacement exceeds its own length, so raise bolt speed from 1.83 px/tick to roughly 4-6 px/tick and cross the 45 px gap in 8-11 ticks instead of 24. (3) Trail: length = min(px travelled since spawn, cap) drawn strictly behind the head, so it starts at zero and can never extend back through the caster. Then re-run the same strip and assert the leading edge advances on every sampled tick.

other_gaps: The shooter is erased by its own shot. Caster body pixels in its authored palette go from 207 at t=71 to 0 at t=74, and stay at 0 through t=77 and t=80 - the additive blob covers the silhouette for the entire discharge. The one frame that says 'this enemy just fired at you' is the one frame where you cannot see the enemy. Gungeon's flashes sit at the barrel tip and never cover the shooter's body. Fix: draw the burst behind the enemy sprite in z-order, offset it to the muzzle rather than the entity centre, and cap its additive contribution so the robe's authored colours survive the frame.

The fire burst has no direction. At t=74 the burst is bilaterally symmetric about its own centre - equal mass fore and aft - and measures 40 px wide by 23 px tall, i.e. taller than the 16 px enemy sprite. A radial shape at the exact instant the player must read 'which way is this going' gives no vector. Reference muzzle flashes are asymmetric cones with the mass thrown forward. Fix: 3:1 forward-to-back mass, height no more than about 8 px, long axis on the aim angle.

The telegraph fades out instead of committing. Lane dot count runs 44 (t=66), 41 (t=68), 28 (t=70), 18 (t=72) - the warning is at 40% of its peak on the last frame before the shot - and its near end retreats from x=62 to x=76, so the ray visibly withdraws toward the wall just before firing. That reads as the threat leaving. Gungeon tells resolve INTO the attack. Fix: hold dot density flat through the aim, then in the final 4 ticks collapse the dotted ray into a solid 1 px line and rim-flash the caster white for 2 ticks so the last pre-fire frame is the loudest.

The warning and the live shot are the same two colours. The telegraph dots are exactly (209,7,209) and (236,71,237), which are the bolt's own palette entries, and the caster's robe sits at (189,56,189) - within ~20 units of both. Three different meanings (enemy body / dangerous soon / dangerous now) share one hue. Gungeon separates them by ownership and liveness: red laser sights vs white-cored yellow and green live rounds. Fix: keep magenta for the telegraph, and give the live bolt a distinct hue (or at minimum a 2x value gap and a white core that the telegraph never uses).

Zero camera or shooter recoil on the discharge. Matched against a fixed prop, the frame offset is (1,-2) at t=71, t=74 and t=77 - identical across the fire tick, and the only movement across the whole strip is a slow 1-2 px camera-follow drift. At 480x270 a 0-px kick is no kick. Fix: 1-2 native px kick along the negative aim vector for 2 ticks with a 3-tick settle, computed in integer native pixels, not a fractional multiplier.

Killing the bolt is quieter than firing it - the inverse of last round's gap, now on the other end. At t=81 the cut splash is about 21 native magenta px; by t=82 the bolt family is 0 px with no residue at all, while the sword arc holds 426 px above L=0.72. The player's skill moment pops out of existence inside a 4-tick hitstop that exists specifically to show it. Reference impact puffs are at least as large as the projectile that made them. Fix: a cut burst of at least the bolt head's own pixel budget, in the bolt's palette, living 4-6 ticks so it outlasts the freeze, plus 3-4 shards thrown back along the incoming vector.

Composition is lane-flat. Caster, bolt, player and the crown pips all sit on one horizontal line through the middle of the crop, and the fire burst - the focal point - is itself mirror-symmetric, so the strongest frame has no asymmetry with intent. The room's own asymmetry (the diagonal cast shadow, the tan prop bottom-right) is the only thing carrying composition, and it is at the frame edge. Fix: offset the burst vertically off the lane axis by a few px and let the trail sag or curve slightly so the fight silhouette is not a straight rule across the frame. (Some of this is the harness pinning both actors to y=121; a capture that does not force the lane would test it honestly.)

Density: the frame carries 2 actors, 1 projectile and about 30 near-white 1 px motes, against reference frames running 30+ simultaneously readable elements. Whole-frame diff between t=56 and t=59 is unchanged from the camera-drift baseline - the background contributes nothing per second. Also, those white motes are 1 px specks scattered across the same lane rows as the 1 px magenta telegraph dots, so two particle systems with opposite meanings are competing at the same size. Fix (particle lane, not the arena lighting lane which already owns the static-light finding): drop the motes to a dim blue-grey, keep them off the danger lane, and draw them behind actors.

biggest_gap.element: The caster's bolt at ticks 74-80 (strip.png cells #08-#10, exhibit.png). Measured at native scale off strip.png: the bolt renders as a wedge that is THICKEST at the caster and tapers outward - column pixel-heights at t=74 run 16,18,15,16,15,13,13,11,11,11,10,10,9,8,7,7,7 from x=70 to x=84. It never detaches: scanning right from the caster's 16px sprite box (crop x 53-69), the first empty column is x=85 at t=74, x=82 at t=77, x=93 at t=80 - a continuous bridge of effect pixels from the shooter's body to the bolt front in every single frame. And it does not travel: the mass strictly right of the caster has centroid x = 76.0 / 74.7 / 76.2 at t=74/77/80, net +0.2 px over six ticks, while the trace moves the bolt 11 px (world 172 -> 184.8 by t=81). Its area is flat too: 205 / 218 / 206 magenta px - no decay over 9+ ticks. At t=74 the discharge also completely covers the caster: you cannot see who fired. So the threat has no head, no gap, no travel and no decay. It reads as a beam the caster is holding, not an object crossing the room - which also means there is no single readable contact frame for the shot, just a 9-tick plateau.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-density-02 downsampled to native 480x270, every enemy bullet is a compact ~7px round white head with a hard 1px rim, sitting at a clearly separated point on a thin 1-2px trail; consecutive heads sit ~11px apart, so displacement is unmissable frame to frame. In ref-density-01 the rocket is a ~5x8 head with a 1-2px white smoke trail, and the blue orb is a 5px round - nothing is welded to its shooter, and the shooter stays fully readable. The reference rule is consistent: the HEAD is the brightest, most compact, most detached element and the trail is thinner and dimmer behind it. Our wedge inverts that - brightest and fattest at the origin, tapering toward the target.
biggest_gap.fix: Split the one effect into three. (a) Muzzle flash: its own burst at the caster's hand that decays to zero over 2-3 ticks and is clipped so it never covers the caster's 16px silhouette. (b) Bolt head: a compact shape no wider than ~6 native px, the brightest thing in the effect. (c) Trail: capped in length and at most 1/3 the head's luminance, with the hard requirement that an empty column opens between the caster sprite box and the bolt within 3 ticks of firing - re-run the column scan above as the gate. Then make motion visible: at 110 px/s the head advances 1.83 px/tick, less than one 2x-scaled pixel, and the 34px trail is 19x that displacement, so the travel is buried. Either raise bolt speed until the head centroid advances >=3 px/tick, or increase the caster's stand-off so the flight is long enough to read, and verify by re-measuring the head centroid per tick - the pass condition is monotonic, not the +0.2 px it measures now.

other_gaps: EVIDENCE LIMIT, stated up front: exhibit B is three stills, so timing cannot be compared against it at all. Axis 3 below is judged only against the stated acceptance criteria, using our own tick-labelled strip.png and the sidecar event trace. I did that and say so plainly. Everything I attribute to the reference is a still-frame property (shape, size, separation, value), never a timing property.

Cutting the bolt - the whole point of this enemy - has no payoff. exhibit-cut.png at t=81 carries 13 magenta pixels in the entire native frame, and a 10px-radius disc around the trace's cut point (world 184.8,121) contains ZERO magenta pixels. A 200+px mass is deleted into nothing. ref-density-01 gives an impact a discrete event of its own: concentric orange rings plus scattered spark dots at the point of contact, separate from both shooter and target. Fix: give boltCut its own burst - 6-10 magenta shards on a radial spread plus a one-tick white core at the blade/bolt intersection, living 4-6 ticks - so the parry frame differs from a whiff frame by something present, not only by the bolt's absence.

The contact frame occludes what it hit. At t=81 the largest single flat-white component (L>0.6, saturation<0.12) is 238 px spanning 25x23 native px against a 16px character, and its bbox x31-55 / y27-49 contains the cut point at (54.8, 40). The one frame that has to show the parry covers it with opaque white. Reference impacts read through: in ref-density-01 the red boss stays fully legible under the flame and smoke burst on top of it, because the burst is ringed and gappy rather than a solid fill. Fix: cap the arc, and make it a ring or a punched-out crescent rather than a solid fill, so the target and the cut point survive the frame that matters most.

The light has a plateau, not a peak. Every frame - quiet t=71, fire t=74, cut t=81 - has max luminance 0.940. Nothing in this piece ever reaches white. Meanwhile 1.36% (fire) and 1.90% (cut) of pixels sit AT that 0.94 ceiling, versus 0.31% and 1.10% above 0.90 in ref-density-01 and -02, both of which do reach 1.000. So we spend more area at the top than the references do and still have no apex: the discharge core, the sword arc and the hit spark all clamp to the same value, and none of them can out-rank the others. Fix, staying inside this lane and off the arena lane's assigned grade item: let the event-owned cores (bolt head, hit spark) clamp to 255 so the event, not the plateau, owns the top step.

The bolt is continuous-tone over a hard palette. The 440-px effect blob in exhibit.png uses 38 distinct colours including 1-unit neighbour steps (111,15,117 / 112,15,117 / 118,20,127 / 120,21,128 / 121,21,128 / 122,22,130 ...), while a 20x30 wall region in the same frame uses 22 - an authored ramp. The card body has no material. Interior is three values across 189 px (12,15,22 at the top falling to 9,10,17 at the bottom) and whole interior rows measure std 0.000. The border is a single 1px stroke, one hue, with only a top-to-bottom brightness fall (136,112,70 down to 102,85,57). Reference surfaces carry grain, modeled bevel, and falloff - its stone panels have carved depth, its meander border is a relief. Fix: give the card a substrate - a 1px inner bevel (light top-left, dark bottom-right), a dither/grain quantised to the 16px pixel scale rather than a soft full-res gradient, and ornamented corner pieces so the frame is a made object rather than a rectangle stroke.

Reading order fights the hierarchy. Measured ink luminance: gate icon 224.7, 'BEGIN AGAIN' 196.5, headline 'NOT YET REBORN' 180.5, and the decorative hairline rule directly above the headline also 180.5 - the exact same ink, (210,179,109). Stat rows 148.6. Subtitle 105.5, contrast 3.55:1 on the card body. So a purely ornamental divider is exactly as loud as the display headline, a purely ornamental icon is the brightest object in the whole frame, and the only text below 4.5:1 is the line that carries the tone. In the reference, brightness IS the hierarchy - the flaming skull and the impact burst are the brightest things and the eye lands on them first. Fix: drop both rules two steps to roughly 110-120 luminance, keep the headline at the top of the ramp with the icon supporting rather than out-shouting it, and lift the subtitle above 4.5:1.

The card moves while you read it. Panel top edge, native: y=62 at t=606-615, y=54 at t=618-621, y=42 at t=654 - with height fixed at 189 px throughout, so this is pure translation, not growth. The headline slides 20 px upward (7.4% of frame height) across 48 ticks as each staggered stat row pushes the vertically-centred layout up. Fix: reserve the final content box before the reveal begins and fade rows into fixed slots. The panel frame must not move at all after t=606.

The scale-in snaps; nothing overshoots anywhere in the sequence. Panel width by tick: 92 (t597), 148 (t600), 204 (t603), 222 (t606) - deltas 56/56/18, a decelerating ramp that terminates exactly at 222 and never exceeds it. The acceptance criterion asks whether recovery overshoots and settles rather than snapping; measured, it snaps. Fix: overshoot the scale by 4-6% around t=604 and settle back over 4-5 ticks, and give the headline a small counter-move of its own so the two elements do not arrive as one rigid block.

Composition is dead centre on both axes. Panel spans x 129-350, centre 239.5 in a 480-wide frame whose centre is 239.5 - zero offset. Vertically 42-231, centre 136.5 against the frame's 134.5, so 2 px BELOW centre, meaning not even an optical lift. Inside, the icon, rule, headline, subtitle, second rule and button all sit on the same single centre axis. The reference composes on a strong diagonal with an unmistakable off-centre focal point and deliberately unequal masses. Fix: lift the card 6-8 px above the geometric centre for optical balance, and break the internal stack - left-anchor the headline block against the icon, or hang the stat rows off one left rule instead of centring everything.

Two hues carry the entire frame. Saturated-pixel hue histogram in 12 bins: 91% blue-violet, 2.7% gold, and literally zero pixels in the other ten bins. The reference runs green, red, orange, cyan and purple simultaneously at mean saturation 119-133 across a full hue spread, and uses that opposition to separate depth planes. Fix: give the death state a second, opposed light source - a cold rim spilling from the gate against the warm gold of the frame - so the image makes a colour argument instead of running one ramp.

Dead HUD chrome outranks the modal. Outside the card, the bottom room label 'THE THRESHOLD' peaks at luminance 41.9 and the top-right WAVE banner at 48.6, both brighter than the card's own body at 14.4. So the two loudest things outside the modal are run-state chrome that no longer means anything - and the WAVE banner is a literal duplicate, since the card already prints 'WAVE 1/1' as its first stat row. Fix: fade the run HUD out entirely as the card comes in, or drop the banner and let the card own that fact.

Originality: the card is a generic results modal - centred icon, rule, display headline, subtitle, leader-dot stat rows, keycap button. That is web/UI-kit vocabulary, not this game's. The reference's UI vocabulary is drawn entirely from its own world: Greek meander, carved stone, skull filigree, so a panel could not be lifted out and dropped into another game. Fix: derive the card's frame from the arena's own tileset. The doorway arch currently sitting INSIDE the card as a decorative picture should BE the card's frame - the player reads the run summary through the threshold he failed to cross, and the leader dots go away in favour of something the room already knows how to draw.

biggest_gap.element: The gate arch inside the death card and the plate it sits on (arch native x213-268, y46-101; card x128-351, y40-229 in the 480x270 frame). It is the piece's own narrative object and it is drawn as a hole, not a light.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-ui-01 every focal object is a light source with a hot core and a multi-stop falloff that lifts AND tints the surfaces around it: the green fire pools and the orange flame run to L=255 and visibly raise the floor tiles for 60-100px in every direction. That frame carries mean L=62.7, p99=238, and 5.28% of pixels above 72% luminance (ref-ui-02: mean 37.2, p99=225, 1.99%).
biggest_gap.fix: Make the arch the only light source on the card and let it spill. Measured now: the arch interior is L=10.0, DARKER than the plate around it at L=14.1; the plate 12px left of the arch reads 14.26 and the plate 70px away reads 14.39 - a 0.13-level difference, i.e. mathematically zero falloff; the gold frame is a flat 114 stroke with no gradient along its run; whole-frame p99 is 130 with 0.12% of pixels above 184. Fill the arch interior ABOVE the plate (target L 40-70, rising to a 200+ band at the threshold line) and paint a 3-4 stop dithered falloff onto the plate over ~40px so the plate directly under the arch reads 25-30 while the card's bottom corners stay at 10. Bias the gold rules brighter on the edge that faces the arch. Gate: frame p99 >= 200 and >= 1.0% of pixels above 184, with that mass in the arch, not in the 1px border.

other_gaps: EVIDENCE LIMIT (stated as required): both reference exhibits are stills, so axis 3 cannot be compared against them. Every timing claim below is measured from our own tick-labelled strip.png and its trace JSON, judged against the feel-chain acceptance criteria only.
AXIS SCORES (0-5) for exhibit B: 1 Readability 3 | 2 Material and light 1 | 3 Feel chain 3 | 4 Composition 2 | 5 Pixel integrity 4 | 6 Density 2 | 7 Originality 4.

FEEL-CHAIN VERDICT against the acceptance criteria (own strip, not the stills): ONE readable contact frame - PASS (burst + full-screen red wash at t=594, gone by t=597). Peak on the damage tick - PASS (events playerHurt,playerDeath both fire at t=594, which is the burst frame). Anticipation distinguishable from idle - PARTIAL. Freeze long enough - MARGINAL. Overshoot and settle - FAIL.

No overshoot on the card entrance. Measured border widths: 150px (t=609) -> 206 (t=612) -> 224 (t=615) -> 224 (t=618) -> 224 (t=621) -> 224 (t=654). Monotone growth, then pixel-identical from t=615 onward - it eases out and snaps to rest. Fix: peak at 232px around t=614 and settle back to 224 by t=620. That is +8px on a 480px frame = 1.7% = half a 16px tile, computed rather than eyeballed, so it is an actually visible overshoot and not a sub-pixel no-op.

The protagonist is deleted rather than killed. At t=594 the burst covers the player; from t=597 the player sprite is simply absent and never returns - no death pose, no collapse, no dissolve - even though the trace has state 'dead' with stateTick counting 0,2,5,8,11... From t=597 to t=606 the frame reads as an ordinary lit room containing only the brute. One frame no longer tells you what happened. Fix: hold a death pose or an 8-12 tick dissolve anchored at the last position (152.6, 38.4) so the beat before the card still has a subject.

Twelve ticks of near-silence between the killing blow and the card. Freeze ends about t=598; the card's first pixel appears at t=606. Across t=597-603 the room's mean luminance moves only 22.2 -> 21.2 -> 20.1 (-9% over 100ms) and nothing else changes. Fix: start the dim on the freeze frame and make it decisive (mean 22 -> 12 across t=598-606), or pull the card's first frame forward to t=600.

The run-ending event carries the same freeze weight as any hit: freeze=4 at t=594 and freeze=1 at t=597, so the hitstop ends about t=598 - roughly 6 ticks, 100ms. Long enough to see a hit, not long enough to register a death. Fix: give playerDeath its own 14-18 tick freeze and hold the red wash across it instead of clearing it by t=597.

The card is a mirror. 83.9% of its pixels are identical to their own left-right mirror image; it is centred at x=239.5 of 480 and y=134.5 of 270 - dead centre on both axes - and is exactly 224px wide, i.e. 14 x 16px tiles. The arch, the divider rule, the title, the subtitle and the keycap all share one centre axis; only the dot-leader stat rows break it. Fix: push the arch off axis and give it a light direction, set the title against the left rule, and take the card width off the tile multiple.

The arena is erased, not dimmed. Outside the card every pixel sits between L=7 and L=37 (room-left p99 12, room-right p99 19); the reference stills keep their periphery readable at p99 193 (ref-ui-01) and 126 (ref-ui-02). The brute that killed you is invisible on the card frame. Fix: dim the arena to ~35-45% instead of ~12% and keep the killer's silhouette legible behind the plate.

The modal has one elevation. Cross-section at y=130 going right: room 7.7 / border 114.1 / 1px gap 10.2 / flat fill 13.1, with the room outside holding a uniform 7.7 for at least 10px - no cast shadow, no ambient occlusion, no second frame. The only depth cue is that the top and left rules are 114.1 while the bottom and right are 86.6 and 97.9. Fix: add a 2-3px cast shadow under the bottom-right (room 7.7 -> 4 -> 6 -> 7.7) plus an inner 1px lowlight rule so the plate reads as an object with thickness.

The plate's vertical gradient is authored but below threshold: six discrete bands from L=14.87 at the top to L=10.29 at the bottom. That is 4.6 levels out of 255, under 2% of range - invisible at any viewing distance. Fix: widen it to roughly 25 -> 8 so the plate has a top-lit face.

The killing burst is a 22-step soft radial gradient rendered at 1px resolution over 16px tiles - gloss over hard pixels. Fix: cut it to 4-5 hard bands with the dither boundary sized to the tile scale, not to the screen pixel.

Two of the three stat rows carry no unit or legend: 'SENT ONWARD 1' and 'HELD 0:09' cannot be decoded on first read, and only 'WAVE 1/1' self-explains. Fix: name the metric ('SOULS SENT ONWARD', 'TIME HELD') or add a one-word unit at the right of the leader.

The live HP capsule top-left stays on the death frame as an empty mid-grey container reaching L=37 - brighter than the entire dimmed arena around it - so the second-brightest object on the screen is a widget carrying zero information. Fix: fade the live HUD down to the arena's dim level, or drain the capsule to the plate's black.

biggest_gap.element: The death card's plate itself — the panel rect at native (128,42)-(351,231), 224x190. Measured off exhibit.png downsampled to native 480x270: the panel fill has a median luminance of 13/255; the scrimmed world just outside it has a median of 7.7/255. The card is separated from the room by 5 luminance units — 2.1% of the range — plus a single 1px hairline (top edge 114, bottom edge 86). There is no cast shadow: the 7 rows below the bottom border read 7.7, 9.0, 10.3, 11.8, 10.0, 7.7, 7.7 (that is room content, not a shadow) and the 7 columns left of the left border read a flat 7.72 all the way out. And the fill is translucent, not a plate: at normal exposure the room's shelf edges and a wall crack read straight through the card, crossing under the gold divider and behind the SENT ONWARD row. Whole-frame tone: p50=8, p90=18, p99=130, max=225, and only 0.12% of pixels above 72% luminance.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: ref-ui-02 is the quietest, darkest frame in the reference pair — a solemn hall, no combat — and it still measures p50=25, p90=87, p99=225, with 2.00% of pixels above 72% luminance. Ours is 3x darker at the median, 5x darker at p90, and carries 1/17th the count of lit pixels; our single brightest pixel in the entire frame (225) only just reaches the reference's p99. Every framed object in both references — the boon doorway, the Mask of Nyx panel, the shrine plinths — is an opaque painted surface stacked in at least three layers: a dark cast shadow separating it from the ground, a heavy mid-value metal frame, and an inner bevel with a lit top edge and a dark bottom edge. The object reads as a physical thing sitting in front of the room, and it owns the top of the frame's value range. Ours reads as a hairline drawn on the room.
biggest_gap.fix: Make the card an object, not an overlay. 1) Kill the translucency — fill opaque so no room geometry crosses the card; nothing behind it should be recoverable at any exposure. 2) Lift the plate off the scrim: fill median from 13 to roughly 34-45 while pushing the scrim's side-region median from 7.7 down to ~4, so figure/ground is carried by value (a 30+ unit step) and not by a 1px line. 3) Layer the frame instead of one hairline: a 2px dark ring at luminance ~3 offset 2px down-right as a cast shadow, then the 1-2px gold rail, then a 1px inner bevel — highlight ~150 on the top and left, ~70 on the bottom and right (the existing 114-top/86-bottom split is the right instinct, it just has nothing stacked on either side of it). 4) Give the plate a material: a low-amplitude texture or a top-to-bottom ramp inside the fill so the surface is not one flat swatch. Target: frame p90 clears 60 and 1%+ of pixels above 72% luminance, with the card — not the room's leftover torches — supplying it.

other_gaps: EVIDENCE LIMIT, as instructed: exhibits B are stills, so no timing was compared against them. Axis 3 was judged only against the acceptance criteria using our own tick-labelled strip.png and its trace. Result: anticipation present (a 12-tick dark ramp from t=597 to t=606, side-region mean falling 15.3 -> 11.4, before the card's slit opens) PASS; exactly one contact frame (t=594 is the only red-flash/burst frame, t=597 is already clean) PASS; freeze reads 4 at t=594, 1 at t=597, 0 at t=600, so about 5-6 ticks / 85-100ms — long enough to see, short enough not to stall, PASS; visual peak lands on the damage tick (frame max luminance and the full-screen red both at t=594, the exact tick the trace records playerHurt + playerDeath) PASS; recovery overshoot FAIL, see next item.

No overshoot on the card's entrance — it eases out and stops dead. Measured panel width across the strip: 92px at t=606, 148 at t=609, 204 at t=612, 214 at t=615, 224 at t=618; height 24 -> 96 -> 166 -> 190 -> 190. It never exceeds its final size, and the rect is bit-identical at t=618, t=621 and t=654 (x 128-351, y 42-231). Fix: overshoot to ~1.04x (233x198) around t=616 and settle back to 224x190 by t=622, or overshoot height only so the card 'drops' into place.

The run HUD is never dismissed, and the HP plate becomes an empty box. At t=654 the top-left health plate is a bare 96x28 rounded rectangle with all five pips gone (player at 0 HP) — 7% of the frame width of literal nothing — and it measures mean luminance 21, BRIGHTER than the card's own fill median of 13. The WAVE 1/1 plate top-right still peaks at 130, tying the card's stat labels. Both references dedicate the frame to one subject. Fix: fade the whole combat HUD to 0 over the 12 ticks between playerDeath (t=594) and the card's first slit (t=606), so the card is the only lit thing when it arrives.

The display font's N is broken, on the hero line. The N glyph's diagonal is a 2-3px stub in the upper-left corner only; the rest is two plain verticals, so 'NOT YET REBORN' reads as 'DOT YET REBORD' at a glance, and the same defect hits SENT ONWARD and BEGIN AGAIN. This is the single most emotionally loaded string on the screen. Fix: run the diagonal corner to corner across all 15 rows of the cap height, or thin the verticals by 1px to make room for it.

Decorative ornament ties the headline for brightness. Measured element peaks: doorway icon 225, BEGIN AGAIN label 196, title 180, the gold divider hairline above the title 180, stat values 148, second rule 113, subtitle 105, panel border 114/86. The purely decorative rule sits at exactly the same peak value as the title. Fix: drop the divider to the second rule's tier (~113) and lift the title to 210-230 so the hero line owns the top of the card's range.

Perfect bilateral symmetry, nothing placed with intent. Panel centre x = 239.5 in a 480px frame (dead centre); left text inset 26px vs right inset 27px; the divider's two end-cap diamonds are identical; icon, rule, title, subtitle, rule, stats, button are all one centred stack. Both references are asymmetric by construction — ref-ui-02 pushes the lit doorway off the centre axis and answers it with a dark statue mass on the opposite diagonal. Fix: break one axis on purpose — offset the doorway icon, or run the divider full-bleed to one border and stop it short of the other, or hang the stat block off a left rule with the values ranged right.

Ragged dot leaders in the stats block. The leader dots run on a fixed 4px pitch measured from the label, so the trailing gap before the value is 4px on the WAVE row, 4px on SENT ONWARD, but 7px on HELD — the leader stops 3px short because the row does not divide evenly. Fix: justify the leader to the value's left edge (distribute the remainder) or right-align the dot run to the value column instead of left-marching from the label.

The scrim is a pure value multiply, so the backdrop keeps all its colour. Backdrop saturation MEASURED UP across the ramp, from mean 117 at t=597 to 127 at t=621 — the room loses value but gains relative chroma, so the red wall glow and orange torches still compete with the card's gold. Fix: desaturate the backdrop 40-60% as the scrim ramps, so gold is the only saturated thing left on screen.

Density is near zero once the card lands. The frame is bit-identical between t=621 and t=654 apart from the staggered content reveal — 33 ticks / 0.55s with no motion anywhere: no drift in the icon's starfield, no flicker on the room's torches through the scrim, no pulse on the BEGIN AGAIN prompt. Both references have three or more simultaneous animated systems in a single still (flame, smoke, spirit crowd, projectile trails). Fix: give the card two slow ambient loops — twinkle the starfield inside the doorway, and pulse the R keycap at ~0.5Hz so the one interactive element declares itself.

The R keycap is illegible. The glyph inside the 14x12px box renders as a solid blob at this size — no visible bowl or leg — and the box has no fill, no press state, and no plate, so the only action on the screen is drawn as body text. Fix: use a 5x7 cell for the keycap glyph with a 1px counter, and give the button a real plate (fill plus the same layered bevel as the card) so it reads as pressable.

SEVEN-AXIS SCORES this round (0-5): 1 Readability 3 — the card states outcome, stats and the action, but the broken N and the empty HP box add noise. 2 Material and light 2 — the worst axis; p50=8, no plate, no shadow, translucent fill (this is the biggest gap). 3 Feel chain 3 — 4 of 5 acceptance criteria pass, only overshoot fails. 4 Composition 2 — dead-centre bilateral stack, and the left and right thirds of the frame are empty black. 5 Pixel integrity 4 — clean: integer rect, exact centring on an even frame, structured 3-tone bevel glyphs (24 discrete luminance levels in the title block, no anti-aliasing), rect bit-identical across three sampled ticks, no shimmer. 6 Density 2 — see above. 7 Originality 4 — gold-on-navy threshold doorway, starfield, 'NOT YET REBORN', 'SENT ONWARD / HELD': this is its own bardo language, not Hades cosplay, and no fan of the reference would call it a copy. Do not fix this axis by importing the reference's composition.

biggest_gap.element: The roll's own silhouette. Across roll ticks 0-10 the character is a single held anisotropic squash of the standing sprite - wider head, flatter body, sword laid over - and it never rotates, tucks, leans, or changes limb. An aligned pixel diff from roll tick 2 to roll tick 8 shows only background parallax; the sprite is one frame stretched over 10 ticks, then eased back over 12. Combined with a 24-pixel peak VFX, one frame of the strip cannot tell you a dodge is happening: the pose reads as the character being flattened by a rolling pin while sliding sideways, which is closer to a hurt state than a roll.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: Both reference stills read the whole action from pose alone, with no motion and no label. In ref-melee-01 Zagreus is unambiguously mid-swing and Megaera is unambiguously mid-lunge, each in a dedicated pose with its own weight and direction; the frame tells you what is happening and what will hurt you before you notice any effect layer. Nothing there is the idle sprite under a transform.
biggest_gap.fix: Give the roll real pose keys on the ticks the sim already names - launch (tick 0), tuck (2-4), extend (6-8), plant (11-13) - and drive the sprite through them; delete the uniform squash entirely. Lean the sprite into the travel direction so the pose also carries the heading. The sim already exposes stateTick, so this is an art-plus-lookup change, not a timing change.

other_gaps: Success flash erases the actor. Player outline pixels in the character region drop 254 -> 14 at roll tick 1 (94% of the silhouette gone), are still 48 at tick 2, 82 at tick 3, and are not restored until tick 5 - 5 ticks / 83 ms of an unreadable player at the exact moment the player wants confirmation. Ref-melee-03 puts an explosion across a quarter of the frame and Zagreus's hard outline still sits in front of it. Fix: draw the flash BEHIND the player, cap it near 60% alpha, and punch the player on top as a white-keyed silhouette instead of letting an additive blob composite over him.

Two identical peak ticks on the contact frame. p99 luminance 238/238 and 664/668 bright pixels at t=48 and t=49: the flash plateaus for 2 ticks rather than giving one readable contact frame. Fails the acceptance criterion outright. Fix: one full-intensity tick, then a 3-tick decay ramp (roughly 100%, 45%, 20%, 8%).

The launch tick is silent. Lavender trail = 0 px at roll ticks 0 and 2, first pixels at tick 4, peak 24 px at tick 10. The frame on which the player pressed dodge, and the frame on which i-frames begin, carry zero dodge-specific pixels - the input produces no visual, which is a defect, not restraint. The visual peak lands 10 ticks after the commit. Fix: put the emission peak on ticks 0-1 and decay from there; the burst belongs where the player pressed.

Trail volume is 24 pixels at maximum - 0.018% of a 480x270 frame. Ref-melee-01 carries a tapered crescent, embers, a blood decal, a lit floor tile and a hit spark inside one frame. Fix: a tapered 3-ghost afterimage of the actual sprite plus a ground scuff, on the order of 150-250 px at peak.

Trail geometry is wrong, not just small. It is one flat lavender rectangle at constant colour, detached from the body by a gap of dark pixels, floating at head height rather than hip height, and tinted a hue that appears nowhere else in the room. The reference slash tapers along its length and starts at the weapon. Fix: taper alpha along the length, anchor the head of the streak to the sprite's hip, and tint it toward the room's warm torch light.

Recovery snaps instead of overshooting and settling. Trace dx per tick: 6.4, 6.0, 3.8, 1.3, 0.3, 0.0, 0.0, 0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 0.7, 1.0 - a dead stop held for 3 ticks, then a monotone forward re-acceleration. There is no counter-motion anywhere. Fails the acceptance criterion. Fix: carry 2-3 px past the stop point on ticks 11-12 and pull 1 px back on 13-14, and put a 2-tick vertical squash-and-pop on the plant tick - dodgeEnd fires on roll tick 13 and the frame currently has nothing on it.

The i-frame window has no tell bound to it. i-frames run roll ticks 1-10, but the lavender trail runs roughly 3-11 and the orange ring in the pass-through strip only ticks 3-4. Nothing starts on tick 1 and nothing ends on tick 10, so the player cannot see when they become safe or when they stop being safe - the 2 open ticks (11-12) before landing look identical to the invulnerable ones. Fix: bind one persistent tell (a sprite rim, say) exactly to iStart/iEnd and blink it out on tick 10.

The trace exposes an `iframes` field that reads 0 on all 36 sampled ticks across all three strips, including the roll ticks 1-10 that timing.json calls invulnerable. The window is inferable only from `successfulDodges` flipping 0->1. The next round cannot assert the tell against the number. Fix: publish the live i-frame counter from the harness so the claim is checkable rather than prose.

The roll is axis-aligned. Player y = 118.0 on all 12 sampled ticks; the whole action is a flat +32 px in x, parallel to the tile seams, so the travel hides itself against the grid. Both reference frames put the actor on a diagonal that crosses the floor pattern. Fix: tune and capture the roll on a diagonal as well, and stop treating the horizontal case as the hero frame.

In exhibit.png the row of HP candles is the brightest object in the frame and sits directly above the player's head, so the eye lands on the meter and not on the roll. Fix: move the pips off the character's headroom, or dim them for the duration of the roll so the action owns the top of the range during the action.

Evidence craft: poses.png is 2304 px wide with content ending near 1152 - half the sheet is empty black, and the three pose cells are cropped so the character sits at the frame edge in two of them. Fix: size the sheet to the frames and centre each pose, so the pose sheet is actually usable as a pose sheet.

biggest_gap.element: The dodge trail — the ONLY per-tick visual the 24-tick roll owns (gauntlet/evidence/dodge-roll/w2r1/exhibit.png at roll tick 6, and strip.png ticks 0-22). Measured from the pixels, not eyeballed: it is a single flat quad, 9x5 game px = 23 px, which is 0.018% of a 480x270 frame and smaller than the character's head (character 16 px tall). At roll tick 6 the quad contains exactly ONE colour, (125,113,169) — there is no fade ramp, no taper, no silhouette. It has ZERO pixels on roll ticks 0 and 2, first appears on tick 4, and pops to zero in one tick at tick 12. It floats ~2 px clear of the body at shoulder height instead of lying on the travel line at the feet. Cross-referenced against timing.json: the fastest part of the move is ticks 0-7 (launch push 0.55, then flat committed speed, peak 191 px/s against a 95 px/s run) and the invulnerable window is ticks 1-10. So the game's one motion cue misses the four fastest ticks entirely, and misses the i-frame window by 3 ticks at the front and 2 at the back. Everything else about the roll is the standing sprite squashed.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-melee-01 the committed action's own effect is the largest and brightest shape in the frame: a crescent roughly four character-heights across, with a hard bright leading edge and a tail that feathers through several values into nothing, sitting on a lit floor pool with radial spark lines thrown off the contact point. The action reads from its effect, in one frame, at any distance. Ours reads only from a 23-px flat rectangle that a player would take for a stray UI element.
biggest_gap.fix: Replace the single quad with a ghost stack: emit a copy of the player's own silhouette every tick starting at roll tick 0, keep 4 alive at once, ramp them across 4 authored palette steps from near-white (newest) to the lavender (oldest), anchor them on the travel line at the feet, and let the last ghosts die out across brake ticks 8-12 instead of switching off. Then tie the stack's on/off to the i-frame window exactly — first ghost on tick 1, last gone on tick 11 — so the same effect also states 'I am untouchable' and the open ticks (0, 11, 12) visibly differ from the safe ones.
