Axes 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 were judged against the reference stills.

AXIS SCORES (exhibit B, dodge-roll w2r1) — 1 Readability 2/5; 2 Material+light 2/5; 3 Feel chain 2/5; 4 Composition 2/5; 5 Pixel integrity 3/5; 6 Density 1/5; 7 Originality 4/5. Exhibit A for reference: 5/5/n-a/5/n-a/5/5.

The i-frame window is unmarked on the player itself. timing.json: ticks 1-10 invulnerable, tick 0 and ticks 11-12 open, whole landing (13-23) open. Across all 36 captured frames the player renders with the same palette, the same outline and the same base arc on safe and open ticks alike. 38% of the cycle is invulnerable and no frame says so — worse, the three open ticks INSIDE the roll are indistinguishable from the ten safe ones, which is actively misleading, not merely absent. Stronger: ref-melee-01 states every combatant's state in one read (the struck enemy is blown red, the incoming threat is a lit pink orb). Fix: swap the player's outline and fill to a pale ramp on exactly ticks 1-10 and drop it on tick 11.

No landing beat. Trace: brake to a dead stop at roll tick 12, dodgeEnd fires at 13, landing runs to tick 23 — 11 ticks, 46% of the whole cycle. Measured across strip-landing: the sprite un-squashes over about 4 ticks (13-16) and then holds unchanged through ticks 17-23. Acceptance criterion 'recovery overshoots and settles rather than snaps' FAILS in a third way — it neither overshoots nor snaps, it stops and waits. No stretch past the settled height, no scuff decal, no dust, and freeze:0 on every one of the 36 captured frames. Fix: one tick of stretch past the settled stance on tick 14, settle by 16-17, and drop a 3-4 px ground scuff at the stop point that fades out across ticks 13-20 so the arrival leaves a mark.

The dodge SUCCESS has no reward of its own. In strip-through the `dodged` event fires on roll tick 1 — the earliest possible read, the best play in the system — and the frame at that tick is filled edge to edge by the BRUTE's attack bloom. Nothing in the frame belongs to the player: no flash, no spark, no hitstop (freeze:0 on all 12 frames). The player cannot tell a perfect read from a lucky one. Fix: a 2-3 tick pale flash plus a small radial tick-mark on the player at the `dodged` event, in a value and shape distinct from the attacker's bloom.

The roll pose is the standing sprite squashed, not a roll. At roll tick 6 the head, the sword and the crown of candles are still in their standing arrangement, and the sword stays vertical for all 24 ticks. Nothing rotates, tucks, or leaves the ground; the crown of candles rides through the tumble like a static hat. Stronger: the reference actor commits — body torqued off its axis, weapon leading the motion. Fix: a dedicated 3-4 frame roll (tuck, over, up) with the sword swung down to the trailing side.

Camera judder through the recovery. Measured on a pure-background patch of strip-landing (an actor-free corner, best-integer-shift alignment): the whole world steps exactly 1 game px in x on roll ticks 11, 14, 16 and 20 and 0 px in between, while the player advances only 0.1-0.3 px/tick. The arena crawls under a near-stationary player at an irregular cadence — that is 20% of the frame's pixels changing on a tick where the player moves a tenth of a pixel. Fix: give the camera a deadzone plus a minimum follow velocity so it either holds still or moves at a steady whole-pixel rate.

The trail is facing-inconsistent. Same colour mask, same roll: rolling right (strip.png) peaks at 24 trail px on ticks 6-10; rolling left (strip-through.png) it never exceeds 12 px and only appears on ticks 9-10. The tell is roughly half as strong and five ticks later depending on which way you dodge. Worth re-measuring on a clean capture, but the mask found it on both. Fix: drive the ghost from the roll velocity alone, not from anything facing-dependent.

Light hierarchy in the exhibit still (noting the arena lane already owns the static-lights issue, so this is filed as an observation, not a claim on the gap): exhibit.png measures p50 luminance 13.1 against ref-melee-01's 31.4, and only 1.37% of pixels above 72% luminance against the reference's 1.85%. The lit tiles sit at the top-left, right and bottom-left EDGES of the crop; the character — the focal point — stands in the darkest patch in the middle. The action itself contributes no light at all.

Evidence-package defects that stop this round being fully judgeable. (a) No idle strip was captured, so the acceptance criterion 'is there an anticipation frame distinguishable from idle' cannot be tested from this exhibit — capture the same crop with no input and diff it. (b) The `iframes` field reads 0 on all 36 captured frames, including every tick timing.json calls invulnerable; only the `dodged` event corroborates the window, so the instrument does not back the claim it is being used to support. (c) poses.png is 2304x408 but everything past x=1152 is flat filler (std 2.5) — half the sheet is empty, and the three poses (t4, t9, t15) skip tick 0, the brake and the settle, which are exactly the moments in dispute. (d) exhibit.png is a 96x66 game-pixel crop with no HUD and no enemy, so axis 4 (composition) cannot be compared against a full-screen reference; ship the exhibit as a full 480x270 frame.

biggest_gap.element: The ordinary dodge roll's traversal, roll ticks 1-10 (the invulnerable window) — exhibit.png and strip.png #00-#05. The roll has no world-space motion graphic at all: the whole read is carried by the 16 px actor sprite. Measured across all 24 ticks of strip.png and strip-landing.png, frame max luminance never exceeds 239.6, and every one of the 5 pixels above 230 belongs to the brute walking in at the top of the crop, not to the roll. The roll's own art peaks at 205.1. Mean frame luminance moves 35.1 -> 36.8 over the entire cycle (+0.7%). The only non-body mark the roll makes is a ~6x5 game-px brown smudge at 60-80 luminance, parked at the launch point.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-melee-01 the action verb is a world-space graphic that exists separately from the character: a crescent at full 255 value, roughly 25% of the frame width, with a hard leading edge and a ragged feathered tail. It is the brightest element in the frame, it states direction and speed on its own, and the character sprite never has to carry the read alone. Same in ref-melee-03, where the explosion is a 255-value shape that owns the frame while Zagreus stays a legible silhouette inside it.
biggest_gap.fix: Give the roll its own ground-plane streak, born on roll tick 1 and killed on roll tick 10 so the graphic IS the i-frame readout. Length ~32 px (the measured roll distance), a hard leading edge at the actor and a 3-4 step value ramp back toward the launch point, drawn at the palette's top authored value so it is the brightest thing in the frame for exactly the ticks the player is safe. That fixes three things at once: the invulnerable window becomes visible information instead of a hidden state, one frame states the travel direction, and the roll finally owns the top of the value range during its own event.

other_gaps: FREEZE IS ZERO ON THE ONE MOMENT THAT DESERVES IT. strip-through.png.json reports "freeze": 0 on all 12 ticks, including t=48 where `dodged` fires and successfulDodges goes 0 -> 1. The perfect dodge gets a huge flash but no hitstop. Fix: 2-3 ticks of freeze on the `dodged` event only (never on an open roll), released before the brute leaves attack tick 11 so the counter window stays honest.

TWO MAXIMUM FRAMES, NOT ONE. The acceptance criterion asks for exactly one readable contact frame. strip-through #01 (t=48) and #02 (t=49) are both at the ceiling: 506 and 518 pixels above 230 luminance, p99 238.4 and 238.2. Frame #03 already has the right answer (dither ring, 27 px above 230). Fix: hold the full-value core for one tick only, then step straight to the #03 ring on the second.

THE REWARD FLASH ERASES THE ACTOR. At t=48-49 mean frame luminance jumps 41.7 -> 70.5 (+69%) and the white core covers the player entirely — you cannot see where you are or which way you are facing while the brute's axe is still live in attack ticks 7-8. ref-melee-01 and ref-melee-03 both keep Zagreus a readable silhouette through their brightest sparks and explosion. Fix: composite the flash UNDER the actor and shape it as a rim or ring rather than a filled core.

THE HP PIPS ARE THE BRIGHTEST THING IN THE ROLL'S OWN HERO FRAME. In exhibit.png (roll tick 4, tuckA) the 116 brightest pixels break down as 40 pips at (236,212,95)/(236,158,66) = 208.7 and 167.9 luminance, and the roll art below them tops out at 205.1. The HP readout out-values the action. They are also a bilaterally symmetric 5-across grid-snapped row directly above the head, sitting in exactly the airspace a roll arc needs. The reference puts HP in a corner bar and leaves the actor's airspace empty. Fix: value-cap the in-world pips below the action's peak, or move them off the actor.

PRESENTATION IS NOT TICK-DETERMINISTIC. Tick 101 is captured twice (strip.png #05 and strip-landing.png #00) from an identical sim state (x=190.7, stateTick 10) and the two renders differ: 145 of 1536 pixels in a provably empty floor region, max delta 77/255, and the pip row shifts a full pixel (delta 228). Frame to frame within one strip, that same empty 24x64 floor region flips 100-320 pixels by up to 104/255, on a 4-tick cycle whose phase is not derived from the tick. So a screen-wide random twinkle is running under a roll that produces no twinkle of its own. Fix: seed the mote/grain layer and the pip bob from the sim tick — evidence becomes byte-comparable and the floor stops competing with the action.

THE ROLL GAINS NOTHING ON RUNNING. Their own trace: wholeCyclePxPerSec 94.8 against runSpeedPxPerSec 95, for 32 px of travel bought with a 24-tick (400 ms) steering commit. The roll is speed-neutral, so it is only ever an i-frame button, never a repositioning tool. Hades' dash is unambiguously faster than walking. Fix: shorten the 11-tick landing tail or raise peak speed until the whole cycle beats run speed by a margin you can see.

ANTICIPATION IS ONE TICK. timing.json holds the `launch` key for roll tick 0 only — 16.7 ms — while every other key holds 3 ticks. It is distinguishable from idle in strip.png #00 (coiled, lower, leaning) so it passes the criterion on the still, but at one tick it will not register in motion. Fix: hold `launch` for 2 ticks and take the tick off the 11-tick landing tail, which is the longest and least informative phase.

THE DUST DOES NOT READ. ~6x5 game px, brown, 60-80 luminance sitting on a 13-luminance floor, and it stays at the launch point instead of being kicked backward. At 480x270 that is close to nothing. Fix: throw it along the reverse travel vector as 3-4 pixel-quantized puffs at mid-to-high palette values.

THE TRACE CONTRADICTS THE CLAIMED I-FRAME WINDOW. Every state dump in all three strips reports "iframes": 0, including roll ticks 1-10 that timing.json calls invulnerable. successfulDodges flipping 0 -> 1 at roll tick 1 is the only proof the window exists. A judge cannot verify the window from the artifact. Fix: expose the live dodge invuln count in the state dump.

DENSITY, MEASURED. One reference frame (ref-melee-01) carries: a named boss with a titled bar, three minions, a 255-value slash arc, a blood decal, a hit spark, six boon icons, an HP bar and a currency counter. Our exhibit frame carries: one player, five HP pips, one brown smudge. Fix is not to copy the HUD — it is that a single frame of our signature defensive verb should contain the threat it is dodging. exhibit.png is cropped to 96x66 game px and contains no enemy at all.

AXIS SCORES THIS ROUND (0-5): 1 Readability 2 — the ordinary roll's only tell is a sprite swap, nothing marks the i-frame window, and the perfect-dodge flash erases the actor for 2 ticks. 2 Material and light 2 — roll art peaks at 205.1, below the HP pips at 208.7; frame max 217.7 against the reference's 255. 3 Feel chain 3 — anticipation present, eight genuinely different authored keys, a real plant/absorb/rise overshoot-and-settle, and the visual peak lands on the exact tick `dodged` fires; lost to freeze=0 and two ceiling frames instead of one. 4 Composition 2 — a symmetric grid-snapped pip row is the brightest element and sits in the focal zone. 5 Pixel integrity 4 — verified clean: 0 of 6336 4x4 blocks in exhibit.png are non-uniform at offset (0,0) and all three other offsets break, so it is a true integer-scale capture and the claimed 1-17 degree lean produces no sub-pixel artifacts; one point off for the off-tick noise layer. 6 Density 1. 7 Originality 4 — the tuck-over-and-extend eight-key roll is its own drawing, not a Hades copy, and nothing here imitates the reference's composition.

EVIDENCE LIMIT, STATED: the reference exhibits are stills, so timing cannot be compared against them. I judged axis 3 entirely against the acceptance criteria using our own tick-labelled strips and the timing.json trace, and I say that plainly. Against those criteria the roll passes on anticipation (launch key at tick 0, distinguishable from idle in strip.png #00), passes on recovery (plant 11-13 -> absorb 14-16 two rows lower -> rise 17-20 is a real overshoot and settle, not a snap), passes on peak-on-the-tick (the flash lands on roll tick 1, the first invulnerable tick, the same tick `dodged` fires), and fails on exactly-one-contact-frame (two ceiling frames) and on freeze (zero).

biggest_gap.element: The successful-dodge burst in strip-through.png, roll ticks 1-2 (t=48, t=49). Measured on the native 128x96 crop: a filled ~40x28 px starburst with an opaque near-white core (L=240) sits exactly on the player. At t=48 and t=49 neither the player nor the brute has a single visible pixel of silhouette — the two frames are also near-identical (frac>90% luminance 0.041 then 0.042), so it is one still image held for 2 ticks with no actor in it. It also lifts the WHOLE frame: native median luminance goes 36 -> 53 (+47%) at t=48 and is still 39 at t=49. Add the tick before it (t=47, the press) where the brute's attack telegraph is an opaque orange ellipse painted OVER both bodies, and three consecutive ticks (50 ms) at the decisive moment of the game's core defensive move contain no readable character.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-melee-01 the white slash is a hollow crescent: the bright pixels form a thin directional arc with an empty interior, drawn UNDER the actors. Zagreus's fully-shaded sprite and Megaera's whole body stay 100% readable through the brightest VFX in the frame, and the screen's median luminance never lifts — the burst is local and the room stays dark around it. The brightest pixels point at the target instead of covering it. Same in ref-melee-03: a huge fire bloom, and Zagreus is still drawn on top of it, silhouette intact.
biggest_gap.fix: Draw the dodge reward behind the actors and never over them: replace the filled disk with an open ring/crescent (1-2 px stroke) plus a directional smear along the roll axis, and re-composite the player and the enemy sprites on top with a 1 px white rim so the brightest pixel in the frame lands ON the actor. Cap the core at ONE tick of full brightness and decay it over 2-3 ticks instead of holding an identical frame twice. Delete the frame-wide additive lift entirely (target: median luminance moves less than 5, not 17). Same treatment for the brute's telegraph — make it a floor decal drawn under both bodies, not an opaque fill on top of them.

other_gaps: EVIDENCE LIMIT, stated as required: the Hades exhibits are stills, so no timing was compared against them. Axis 3 was judged only against the acceptance criteria, using our own tick-labelled strips and the JSON traces.

No i-frame tell. iframes run ticks 1-10; ticks 0 and 11-12 are open. Nothing in the sprite changes across that boundary — the palette, rim and shadow are identical at tick 10 (safe) and tick 11 (open). The player has no way to learn where the 10-tick window ends. Worse, strip.png.json reports player.iframes: 0 on every single sampled tick including the invulnerable ones, so the instrument cannot confirm its own key claim. Fix: bind a visible state to the exact ticks — flat 2-colour silhouette + 1 px rim on ticks 1-10, full shading returns on tick 11 — and make the harness emit the real iframes value so the tick can be verified from the trace.

Light hierarchy inverted inside the actor. In exhibit.png the ground-contact bar under the feet measures L=217 — brighter than the torch core (208) and far brighter than the rolling body (91-154, with one 205 face patch). The eye is pulled to a white slab on the floor, not to the person. Hades draws the ground shadow DARK and puts its highest values on the blade and the trail. Fix: take the contact mark below the floor value and move the top of the range onto the helmet and sword tip.

No directional motion cue in a travel frame. The roll covers 32 px at a 191 px/s peak, yet a still at roll tick 4 (exhibit.png, and ticks 0/2/4/6 in strip.png) has no ghost, no smear, no speed line and no dust puff — only the sprite's position between frames says it is moving. Hades' dash reads as motion in one still. Fix: 2 subtractive-alpha afterimages at -1 and -2 ticks along the travel axis, plus a 3-4 px dust puff at the launch foot on tick 0.

Recovery overshoots and never settles. Measured native pixel change in the player band, strip-landing.png: ticks 14->15 = 96 px, 16->17 = 194 px, 17->18 = 204 px (a near-stall), then 18->19 = 1142 px (a jerk). Across ticks 12-22 the body is one unchanging squat blob and only the sword arm rotates from horizontal to ~60 degrees; the state ends at tick 24 with the arm still travelling, so it hands off to idle mid-overshoot. Fix: deepest compression on 14, counter-rise overshoot on 16-17, back on the idle carry pose by tick 20 so the last 4 ticks are genuinely still.

Composition of the hero frame is grid-snapped and bilateral. In exhibit.png (96x66 native) the actor sits at x 39-58, i.e. dead centre, under a row of five identical, evenly spaced torches. Ref-melee-01 puts the fight off the centre third with pillars of different sizes at different depths and the slash arc leading the eye. Fix: reframe so the brute and its telegraph are in shot (a defensive move's hero frame currently shows no threat at all) and push the actor off centre.

Density. At any instant the dodge shows 1-2 moving layers (sprite + ground streak; a burst only on a successful dodge). One Hades frame carries slash arc, blood spray, hit spark, aura, floor decal, damage number, health bar and status ring at once. Fix: layer the roll so no tick has fewer than two moving elements — dust at launch, trail through travel, scuff ring at the plant, sword-tip streak in recovery.

Evidence tooling misrepresents the art. The strips' 3x zoom is not nearest-neighbour: 18.3% of native pixels have an internal range >20 inside their 3x3 block and 8.4% have >40, so every strip a critic reads is a blurred version of the real frame. exhibit.png at 4x measures 0.0% non-uniform, which proves the renderer is grid-clean and the blur is the strip tool. Fix the strip resize to NEAREST; pixel integrity itself is fine (4/5).

Originality. The only signature marks on this piece are the five identical torches and the flat white contact bar, and neither is authored — both are defaults. Nothing here is a copy of Hades, which is right, but nothing yet reads as Bardo either. Fix: give the roll one authored signature (e.g. the cape/cloth trailing a beat behind the body through the tuck) rather than borrowing a composition.
Axis scores this round, 0-5: readability 1, material and light 2, feel chain 2, composition 1, pixel integrity 4, density 2, originality 2.

biggest_gap.element: The charger's dash telegraph in busy.png (charger id 7, state "freeze", stateTick 9, occupying roughly x168-236, y188-215). Measured in render space, the cone's fill sits at luminance 0.313 while the bare floor immediately above it sits at 0.389 - the thing that is about to hurt you is 0.076 DARKER than the ground it lies on. Its mean saturation is 0.100 against the floor's 0.105, i.e. identical. The only saturated pixels are 196 px of 2x2 orange dots outlining the shape - 10.7% of its bounding box - so the lethal area is marked by its border and the interior is left reading as floor. The same holds for the brute's windup at (109,215): a soft brown spiral drawn at the floor's own value, over the player.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-room-01 the danger is the brightest thing in the frame and it is SOLID, not outlined: the laser bands measure 0.482 luminance over a 0.226 floor - +0.256, more than double the ground - with a white core and an additive bloom halo, and every emitter is capped with the same red-orange lamp. One glance sorts harm from decor because harm owns the top of the value range and one saturated hue family. ref-density-01 does the same with projectiles, muzzle flash and shockwave rings.
biggest_gap.fix: Make threat area luminance, not hue-on-outline. Fill the whole telegraph shape, not its border: raise the fill to at least +0.20 luminance over the local floor (floor is ~0.28-0.39, so target 0.55-0.60 inside the cone) at high saturation, with a white or near-white leading edge at the contact boundary, and add an additive glow pass over it. Then apply one telegraph vocabulary to all three threats - charger cone, brute windup, caster aim - so anticipation, contact and lethal area all read from the same colour/value rule instead of three unrelated idioms (dotted orange outline, brown spiral, magenta lozenge).

other_gaps: EVIDENCE LIMIT, stated as required: the reference exhibits are stills, so no timing claim was made against them. Exhibit B also shipped NO tick-labelled strip and NO trace - only two single frames plus state JSON - so the feel-chain acceptance criteria (anticipation frame distinguishable from idle, exactly one contact frame, freeze duration, recovery overshoot, peak landing on the damage tick) COULD NOT BE CHECKED AT ALL. The missing strip is itself the gap: a lane cannot be graded on axis 3 without it. All that is visible is busy-state.json reading freeze:3 with player state "attack" stateTick 6, i.e. hit-stop exists and is 3 ticks (50 ms); whether the visual peak lands on the damage tick is unverifiable from this exhibit.

Seven-axis scores for Exhibit B, w2r1, so round 11 stays comparable: 1 Readability 1. 2 Material and light 2. 3 Feel chain UNSCORABLE (no strip/trace; provisional 2 from the single attack frame). 4 Composition 2. 5 Pixel integrity 3. 6 Density 1. 7 Originality 4.

The hero frames are blank. still.png and exhibit.png render NO arena at all: the region x50-430, y70-230 is a flat fill - the 16x16 px block where the player stands (208,184) has every single pixel at exactly 0.0585 luminance, max = mean, so this is an opaque curtain, not a dim room. Yet still-state.json shows tick 30, wave "active", player state "free" stateTick 30: the sim is live and the player is controllable behind a black screen for the first half-second, while the HUD banner and flame pips render at full brightness on top of it. bible.json's own gates then measure the curtain (floorMean 0.055, top-1% minimum luminance 0.059, centroid (235,18) - inside the HUD banner, 231 px from the declared focal). Stronger: ref-room-02 runs a full dialogue banner over a fully lit, fully drawn room; Gungeon never hides the arena from a player who can move. Fix: end the world fade before input is enabled, or fade HUD and world together, and re-shoot the still - two of the three frames shipped this round carry no judgeable image.

Colour is nearly absent. Pixels above saturation 0.35: ours 0.96% (busy.png) against 4.74% in ref-density-01 and 9.16% in ref-room-01; mean saturation 0.049 vs 0.086 and 0.119; unique colours 3,112 vs 17,629 and 30,755. The arena is functionally greyscale with three accents. Fix: author hue separation into the stone itself (warm torch-side, cool shadow-side) rather than tinting one grey, and push actor and threat colours to the palette ends.

The wave's headline brightness claim does not hold for this frame. busy.png p99 luminance measures 164/255 (0.642), not the 229 quoted for this wave; ref-density-01 measures 203 and ref-room-01 measures 254. Whatever frameStats reported, the arena frame actually shipped is ~40 p99 points below even the darker reference. Fix: re-measure the gate on the delivered PNG, not on a different capture path, before claiming the grade is repaired.

Floor module is wrong scale and wrong material. Mortar lines fall at y = 71, 104, 137, 170, 201 and x = 76, 109, 158, 287, 321, 368, 401 - a 32x32 px running-bond course, i.e. 2x2 gameplay tiles, half-offset row to row: a WALL pattern laid flat, and the same pattern and angle as the actual wall at the top of the frame, so floor and wall read as one surface. Per-24px-block value spread is only std 0.064. Reference floors sit on the same 16 px module as the characters, as square flagstones with visible per-tile value variation, cracks and debris decals. Fix: re-author the floor at 16 px, break the running bond, vary tile value, add decal/debris tiles.

Player silhouette is destroyed by its own FX. At (108.5,200.5) the player, the brute at (109,215.5) 15 px away, a ~48 px soft brown windup spiral, a white sword crescent, a blood decal and a spark burst all stack inside one ~40x40 px area, all drawn at full opacity above the actors. The reference keeps the actor silhouette on top and reads FX around it. Fix: draw actor sprites above ground FX, keep the dark outline unbroken, and reserve the white core for the contact frame only.

The bible's declared focal is stale. bible-busy.json reports focal (312, 184.6) while busy-state.json puts the player at (108.5, 200.5) and the frame's own top-1% centroid at (198, 175) - the declared focal is ~204 px from the actual action, yet topOnePercentLocation still reports pass:true. The gate is scoring against a number nobody updated. Fix: derive focal from the frame's player position at capture time.

Density is roughly 7x short. At 8.4 s with 5 live enemies, busy.png shows four discrete event elements: one impact puff, one bolt, one dash cone, one swing arc. ref-density-01 carries ~30 simultaneously - shell casings, three smoke trails, multiple projectiles, four ring shockwaves, hearts, blood spray, muzzle flash, debris - and every one of them is legible. Fix: add persistent secondary FX (casings/embers that live 1-2 s, ground scorch, shockwave rings on contact) so the frame keeps a history of the last second.

Particles leak outside the room. In busy.png, bright dust streaks render over the black letterbox at (26,135)-(18,143) and (17,205)-(9,213) on the left, plus 66 pixels above 0.3 luminance on the right, all beyond the arena wall. Both references are hard-masked - nothing exists outside the room rectangle. Fix: clip ambient motes to the arena rect.

Composition is an undivided rectangle. The room is one axis-aligned box with props hung near the walls and an empty middle; nothing breaks the perimeter and nothing gives the fight cover or a reason to move to a specific spot. ref-room-01 breaks its rectangle with inset alcoves, raised blocks and pits that create asymmetric sightlines. Fix: add interior cover geometry sized in dodge-distance units so the composition has a focal region other than 'the centre of a rectangle'.

biggest_gap.element: The arena floor itself — its value, its chroma and its detail frequency. Measured in 480x270 render space from busy.png: interior L p50 0.211 with NO pixel anywhere in the frame below L 0.063 (0.00% under 0.05); interior chroma p95 0.094, i.e. 95% of the playfield sits within 9% of neutral grey; and the mortar dither plus the uniform 1px floor speckle push an empty floor patch to a high-frequency energy of 0.215 against the fight zone's 0.243 and a caster sprite's 0.273. The floor has 88% of the edge energy of the combat happening on it, so nothing separates figure from ground. With 5 live enemies on screen (2 casters, a brute in windup 8 ticks from contact, a charger mid-dash, a charger in freeze) I could not identify the brute at all, and could not tell the charger's dash lozenge from the caster's bolt from a prop.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: ref-density-01's floor is near-black, near-flat and near-neutral: L p50 0.083, HF energy 0.029, and 8.66% of the frame at true black (L 0.000). It spends nothing on itself. All the chroma (7.96% of pixels above 0.35 chroma, 8x ours) and all the edge energy (boss zone HF 0.162, 5.5x its own floor) belong to entities and their light, and the saturated pixels cluster tightly on the fight (sd 61x54 px against our 105x85). Zoomed in, a bullet-kin is orange and magenta at chroma 0.7+ with a darker-magenta rim outline sitting on an almost featureless L~0.06 ground: you read every threat in one glance because the ground is silent.
biggest_gap.fix: Three changes to the room shell, each with a number to hit. (1) Pull the grade's black point to 0 and drop the unlit floor's mid-value lift so empty stone away from a light measures under L 0.10 and the frame gets 8-35% of pixels below L 0.05 like both references. (2) Delete the per-tile mortar dither and the uniform 1px speckle scatter so an empty floor patch measures HF energy under 0.08 (from 0.215) — keep texture as low-frequency value blocking, not 1px chatter. (3) Hard-reserve chroma above 0.35 for entities, threats and light sources only: target 3-6% of playfield pixels above that threshold (from 0.97%) with an x-spread under ~65px around the fight (from 105), and give every entity a 1px dark rim so the silhouette survives on any floor value.

other_gaps: Amber is spent on decoration, so the one warm 'this will hurt you' hue reads as furniture. The brute's windup arcs (~#8a6a4a) sit in the identical amber/brown family as the wall torch, the brazier, the wooden props, the room border and the HUD frame. The reference splits hue by function: enemy fire red-orange with a white-hot core, player fire yellow, pickups magenta hearts — three families, never reused for scenery. Fix: give each threat class its own hue plus a white core (brute amber, caster violet/cyan, charger a third), and push every decorative amber below 0.15 chroma.

Entities have no ground contact. The caster at render ~(280,133) stands with nothing beneath it and reads as floating; the chargers and the bolt likewise. Every entity in ref-density-01 is anchored by a soft dark ellipse under it. Fix: one ellipse shadow per entity, radius from the hitbox, alpha from the nearest light.

Vector strokes laid over pixel art. The brute's two windup arcs, the charger's dotted lasso and the bolt's dotted outline are anti-aliased stroked paths with sub-render-pixel dot pitch and soft varying-width ends, drawn over 16px sprites — gloss over placeholder. The reference draws every beam and telegraph as pixel-quantised art on the same grid (ref-room-01's laser beams have hard stair-stepped edges). Fix: snap arc radii, stroke widths and dot pitch to integer 480x270 pixels; no alpha ramp narrower than 1 render px.

The exhibit ships no tick-labelled strip and no trace, only two isolated frames 477 ticks apart. Axis 3 therefore cannot be scored against its own acceptance criteria: I can see freeze=3 and a windup state in busy-state.json, but not whether there is exactly one readable contact frame, whether anticipation differs from idle, whether the freeze reads without stalling, or whether the visual peak lands on the damage tick. Fix: capture a per-tick strip across the swing (roughly windup-6 to recovery+8) with the tick number burned into each frame and the damage-enable tick marked from the trace.

Player HP is read twice in the same frame and the second read sits on the player's head. The top-left HUD shows 3 lit braziers + 2 dark; a second 5-pip strip (3 gold, 2 dark) floats over the player sprite and occludes the swing arc at the exact spot the eye needs during an attack. Both reference room shots keep HP in one corner only. Fix: pick one location; if the world-space read stays, move it off the sprite and show it only on damage.

Chrome renders at full opacity over an unlit void. still.png at tick 30 (0.5 s in) has floorMeanLuminance 0.055 — 21% of the lit value — while the HUD, the WAVE 1 banner, the control-hint bar and 'THE THRESHOLD' are all fully opaque over black; exhibit.png is a crop of essentially nothing. Neither ref-room shot ever puts chrome over an unlit room. Fix: gate the banner and hint bar on the room reaching ~0.15 floorMean, or fade them in on the same curve as the room.

The frame's brightest region does not claim the focal point. bible.json declares focal (312, 184.6); the still's top-1% luminance centroid is (235, 18) — 231px away, inside the HUD band, with fractionWithin64px = 0. busy recovers to 0.922 within 64px, but its top-1% is still smeared sd(130, 85) against ref-density-01's sd(59, 54). Fix: tighten the brightest 1% to a single cluster on the fight and keep chrome out of the top luminance band entirely.

centreLift fails in both frames with deltaBands = 0. busy measures centre60 0.307 against an outer-ring 0.203 — a 0.104 luminance lift that never crosses a band boundary, so the centre of the room, where the fight is, never reads as the lit place. Fix: make the centre-to-edge falloff cross at least one full band, which the black-point fix above largely buys for free.

Silhouette identity is weak across enemy classes. Both casters are the same pink-hooded ~14x16 sprite at the same scale, the charger mid-dash renders as a featureless magenta lozenge, and the brute in windup is an unreadable dark hood mass. The reference gives every class a distinct silhouette, size ratio and colour so class is legible before behaviour is. Fix: differentiate by outline shape and size ratio, not palette alone.

Floor block value varies randomly and independently of the lights. The large stone blocks alternate roughly +/-0.1 luminance in a pattern with no relationship to the torch, the brazier or the room's openings, so the floor reads as blotching rather than as a lit surface. In ref-room-01 every floor and wall value traces back to a visible light. Fix: derive block value from the light field, keep per-block variation under ~0.03.

biggest_gap.element: Enemy sprite lighting in busy.png: every enemy is DARKER than the floor it stands on. Measured Weber contrast against a 3x-radius local background ring: caster1 -0.34 (L 0.052 vs floor 0.079), charger5 -0.34 (0.156 vs 0.236), brute -0.55 (0.060 vs 0.133), caster2 -0.04. Body saturation 0.42-0.48. The brute is winding up (state 'windup', stateTick 8) directly on top of the player and is the least visible object in the frame.
biggest_gap.stronger_does: In ref-density-01 every ordinary threat is brighter than its floor by a Weber contrast of +1.43 to +2.17 (2.4x-3.2x local floor luminance) at body saturation 0.63-0.67, each with a hard dark keyline and a cast contact shadow. Where A does go darker than the floor, it is the boss at -0.17, and it pays for that with saturation 0.96 and a silhouette filling ~12% of the frame. A never asks you to find a low-saturation sub-floor-value sprite.
biggest_gap.fix: Light the actors above the room instead of under it. Give every enemy body an authored value floor tied to the local floor value (target body mid-tone >= 2x local floor L, i.e. >= 0.30 against our 0.15 floor) and lift body saturation into the 0.60-0.70 band A uses. Add a 1px warm rim on the key side plus a hard dark elliptical contact shadow at the feet so the silhouette survives even when the body value dips. Then split silhouette hue per archetype (brute / charger / caster) so the type reads from value and hue, not from a pink hat. Re-measure the same four Weber numbers and require all >= +1.0.

other_gaps: FRIEND/FOE HUE COLLISION. In busy.png my own sword arc has median hue 29deg (sat 0.61), the incoming charger telegraph has median hue 23deg (sat 0.43), and the decorative brazier fire has median hue 12deg (sat 0.84) - three orange shapes at overlapping values, two of which are the thing I did and the thing that will hurt me, sitting adjacent on screen. A codes danger away from the player's own output and away from set dressing. Fix: reserve the orange/amber band for room fire only, move enemy telegraphs to a single reserved danger hue (a hot red-magenta at sat >= 0.8 with an animated inward-collapsing edge), and move the player's arc to a cool white-cyan. Verify by hue histogram: no two of {player output, enemy telegraph, room fire} may share a 30deg bin.

SINGLE FLAT VFX TOP END. The sword arc, the charger telegraph, the caster bolt core and the hit spark all peak at literally the same pixel value: #ECF0F6 (hue 216deg, sat 0.04, L 0.940). The frame never reaches white; the authored ceiling is 6% below it and it is cool blue-grey, so an impact reads grey against warm torchlight. A's muzzle flash has a pure 1.000 white core wrapped in a saturated orange halo, and its bullet tracers, impacts and boss are each a different colour at the top of the range. Fix: give each event class its own 2-3px core-plus-falloff ramp - a true 1.0 white core for the contact frame only, and a hue-tinted (not shared) falloff for arc, telegraph, and bolt. This is about the palette's authored ceiling and the one shared VFX colour, not about which source owns >72% luminance.

FLOOR IS FLAT AND READS AS A WALL. Edge energy |dx| 0.0041 / |dy| 0.0064 against A's 0.0087-0.0117 - roughly half the detail per pixel. Our floor is large single-value blocks in running-bond masonry courses with even seams straight across the full width, so it reads as a wall seen head-on rather than a floor seen from above. A's floors carry 3-4 value variants per tile, cracks, and scattered debris and shell casings that also record what has already happened in the fight. Fix: 3-4 value variants per floor tile, a joint/grout value that varies, and persistent battle litter dropped by combat so the floor remembers the fight. Re-measure edge energy, target |dx| >= 0.0080.

THE HERO FRAME HAS NO FIGHT IN IT. exhibit.png is still.png (tick 30, zero enemies, player idle) with a 'WAVE 1' title card across the play area and a 'WASD MOVE / AIM / STRIKE / SPACE DODGE' key bar laid over the bottom of the room. Both of A's room frames carry a live subject inside the play field - a shopkeeper mid-line under a lit shrine, or a player under crossing laser fire - and keep chrome pinned to the corners. Fix: capture the exhibit on a combat tick, and move wave count and room name into the existing corner chrome so nothing overlays the arena.

LIGHT LIVES AT THE FRAME EDGES. In still.png the entire room interior peaks at L 0.828, while the bottom margin strip (room-name and control-bar chrome, outside the arena) reaches 0.875 - the brightest pixel in the frame is decoration outside the playfield. The pure left margin holds 504 pixels above L 0.3 in drifting dust specks, in a region where nothing can ever happen. The bible's own centre_lift gate FAILS: centre-60% 0.0286 vs outer ring 0.0153, band_delta 0. A's ref-room-02 lights its centre 6.7x above its ring and lets the margins go black. Fix: a real key light on the arena centre that clears the ring by one full band, and cap every non-playfield element below the room interior's peak.

ON-SCREEN SIMULTANEOUS EVENT COUNT. At 8.5 s of live combat (6 swings, 9 hits, 3 kills, 12 enemy attacks) our busy frame shows four live elements: one bolt, one spark, one arc, one telegraph. ref-density-01 shows roughly eight projectiles and tracers, three impact clusters, two smoke plumes, six loose pickups and ~20 debris pieces at once - about 4x our per-frame event load, and much of it is persistent residue rather than more instantaneous events. Fix: make impacts leave debris, scorch and casings that persist for seconds, and raise the number of bolts alive concurrently, rather than raising the event rate.

EVIDENCE PACKAGE CANNOT SUPPORT AXIS 3. The folder ships three stills and two state dumps; both dumps report freeze: 0, and there is no tick-labelled strip and no trace. None of the five feel-chain acceptance questions (anticipation frame distinguishable from idle, exactly one contact frame, freeze long enough to see and short enough not to stall, recovery overshoot-and-settle, visual peak on the damage tick) can be answered from it. Fix: ship a tick-labelled strip spanning windup through recovery plus the damage-window trace alongside the stills, and diff the action strip against an idle strip so a no-visual input registers as a defect rather than as restraint.

COMPOSITION IS A CENTRED RECTANGLE. The arena is a perfectly centred bordered box with near-equal margins on all four sides and a uniform grid of same-size blocks inside. A's ref-room-02 pushes its light source and its subject off-centre and breaks the grid with an L-shaped floor edge and a diagonal ledge. Credit where due: mirror asymmetry is now 0.0231 rather than zero, so the left-right mirroring is genuinely fixed. Fix: one asymmetric architectural feature - an off-axis alcove or a broken floor edge - so the room has a near side and a far side.
